data.title: Four Years of Jai (2024)
data.author: xixixao
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了编程语言Jai的优缺点以及作者四年来的使用经验。作者是一位经验丰富的程序员，接触过多种语言和框架，如C、C++、Java、Python和JavaScript等。文章首先回顾了软件性能在硬件快速发展背景下逐渐变差的趋势，原因包括CPU架构变化、脚本语言的流行、以及面向对象编程等方法论的局限性。

Jai语言以其媲美C的性能和现代编程习惯为目标，试图成为C++的强大替代品，同时注重提升程序员的开发体验。作者在2020年加入Jai的Beta测试，并已在专业项目中使用三年。文章从高层次概述、优点、缺点、专业使用、Beta状态和未来发展等多方面进行分析，尽管Jai仍在封闭测试中，作者对其前景持积极态度。

总的来说，Jai在性能和开发体验间取得了较好平衡，但其长期发展仍待观察。

主要讨论点：Jai编程语言的特性、开源与否、与其它语言的比较以及实际应用

不同观点：
• [sph] 认为Jai作为封闭源码语言不值得投入学习，特别是在现代不再像90年代那样接受封闭软件。尽管目前处于封闭alpha阶段可以理解，但希望最终能开源或作为自由软件发布。同时关注Jai在系统编程方面的能力，例如是否容易写内核、是否支持内联汇编和自定义链接阶段等。

• [VyseofArcadia] 批评当前软件对硬件性能的浪费，指出在过去10-20年间硬件进化被软件低效抵消。认为行业应更关注效率问题，特别是在应用程序和操作系统层面。

• [TinkersW] 对Jai的开发团队对RAII（资源获取即初始化）机制的理解表示怀疑，并指出C++程序的重建时间不应过长。对Jai的元编程和部分设计选择（如使用字符串表示"sin"/"cos"）感到困惑，认为文章未能清晰展示Jai的优势。

• [mppm] 认为Jai长期处于封闭测试状态令人不解，一方面理解开发者不想被外界干扰，但另一方面这也浪费了关注者的精力和时间，导致知识被逐渐遗忘。

• [sesm] 指出async/await模式在JS中更多是为了代码可读性，而非性能。

• [pcwalton] 回应关于内存安全的讨论，指出如果不想使用垃圾回收，就必须在编译器复杂性或语言限制之间做出权衡，认为不可能存在没有任何缺点的系统。

• [lifthrasiir] 认为Jai的问题在于它像开源语言一样启动却未真正开源，导致困惑和失望。指出许多其他语言在测试阶段仍保持开源，并认为Jai没有实际理由继续保持封闭。

• [kbr-] 质疑Jai通过defer机制取代RAII的可行性，指出在某些情况下（如将需要清理的资源对象放入向量并转让所有权）destructor的重要性。

• [perching_aix] 反问如果将复杂性放入编译器，那么编译器将如何工作，质疑是否存在魔法或 clairvoyance。

• [malkia] 提到Jai的线程上下文栈设计类似GoLang的context，认为这种设计在多线程编程中是必要的。

• [spacechild1] 质疑匿名函数在JS中是否会导致内存分配。

• [phtrivier] 担心在Jai发布时人们可能已经转向Zig或Rust，导致Jai变得 irrelevant，但也希望这种担忧是错误的。

• [IshKebab] 认为Jai难以与Zig竞争。

• [sushidev] 希望文章中有更多代码示例。

• [msmshazan] 关注Jai何时会进入开放测试阶段。

补充讨论：
• Jai的开源状态和其与Zig、Rust的竞争关系是主要争议点。
• 对Jai在系统编程和性能优化方面的能力存在不同看法和期待。
• 部分评论对Jai的特定设计选择（如元编程、字符串表示函数）感到困惑。
• 对内存管理和RAII机制的不同理解和偏好也是讨论的焦点。

Contents
Four Years of Jai
SmÃ¡ri McCarthy
2024-12-02
6335 words
30 minutes
Contents
I’ve been programming for long enough to be righteously cantankerous about a lot of things. The list of languages, frameworks and libraries I’ve worked with professionally or on personal projects is too long to list – but it includes everything from C and assembly languages through C++, Pascal and Delphi, through Java and Clojure, through Perl, PHP, Python, Javascript, Typescript and so on. I’ve tinkered with Rust, APL, Uiua, Erlang and Haskell. I’ve been around the block a few times.
So let me just open this discussion by saying: I’ve seen the good, the bad and the ugly, and I know how big the “ugly” category is – how ridiculously small the “good” category is.
Which is why, when I first heard of Jai, I was intrigued. The central focus made sense: a language of comparable performance to C, but with modern idioms, conveniences and tooling – a language aiming to be a powerful alternative to C++ in environments where performance is everything, while emphasizing the importance of programmer morale. This seemed like music to my ears, and I followed the occasional updates for years.
Then, in early 2020, I got invited to join the Beta. From what I could tell I was about the 20th-or-so person to join it.
Now it’s four years in, and further, even though it’s still in closed Beta (I’ll come back to that), I have been using Jai professionally for the last three years – a decision which could be considered controversial, but I’ll address that in this essay.
What I’m going to cover here is:
The high level overview
Things I like
Things I don’t like
Using Jai professionally
The status of the Beta
The road forward
But, this essay will also be 0-indexed:
0. The lost era of good software
Software has been getting slower at a rate roughly equivalent to the rate at which computers are getting faster.
The causes of this are manifold. Some of it is attributable to the maxim that became popular in the 90’s, that software developers were more expensive than faster hardware, so they should be encouraged to not waste their time writing good code if bad code written quickly will suffice.
Part of it is due to architectural changes made to CPUs around 1999, which introduced a layered CPU cache system, broke a lot of assumptions that had held true for decades up until that point. In particular, CPUs and RAM used to have roughly equivalent clock speeds and fetching data from RAM would take 1-2 CPU cycles, so it wasn’t very expensive. But as the clock speeds diverged and RAM grew in size, these diverged – now it can take up to 200 CPU cycles for a memory read to return. As a result, caching is more important than ever, and many things that weren’t bad before, or even actively encouraged, such as linked lists where each item is randomly allocated on the heap, are now insanely expensive.
Some if it is compounded by the development, in particular since the early 90’s, of scripting languages that are meant to be used for everyday software development – the likes of Perl, Ruby, Python, PHP and Javascript. What these brought to the table was a sense of “high level”-ness; that you could write code in a way that was abstracted away from the particulars of the underlying architecture by way of a bytecode interpreter or a virtual machine, or in some cases a just-in-time compiler. This presented many benefits, in particular a reduced need to be concerned with resource management, a task relegated to a garbage collector or such. Suddenly programmers were being encouraged to pretend they knew nothing about the hardware their program was destined to run on. Just assume that resources are abundant, that their allocation and deallocation was practically free, and if things started getting sluggish they could just ask management for more servers.
This came at a cost, but in many cases the efficiency hit was easily justified. Some languages went as far as to make the case that the efficiency tradeoff itself was a feature: that the existence of a virtual machine that hogged memory and reduced your code execution speed made it more “portable”. “Write once, run anywhere,” they claimed, except in practice it was never quite all that.
Some of the slowdown comes due to various ideologies and methodologies, including but not limited to
Object Oriented Programming
, RAII (Resource Allocation Is Initialization) and
Clean Code
having turned out to be conceptual traps which provided a sense of achievement and righteousness, justified by terms like “zero cost abstraction”, “encapsulation” and “cleanliness” which in practice had huge performance hits, and a host of other issues, associated with them.
And some of the slowdown comes because programming paradigms have largely failed to keep up with the rapid expansion from single-core to multi-core and multi-threading. Many of the general purpose concurrency and parallelism models being pushed turn out to have unintuitive performance bott

data.title: A New ASN.1 API for Python
data.author: woodruffw
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了ASN.1在加密学、网络协议和Python中的重要性及其面临的挑战，并宣布了一个新的ASN.1 API开发计划。ASN.1是一种数据结构描述语法，广泛应用于TLS握手、X.509证书验证、LDAP、SNMP等核心网络协议中。然而，其历史上有许多内存损坏和拒绝服务漏洞。当前Python中的ASN.1库（如pyasn1）性能不足，且容易导致解析差异风险。

为了解决这些问题，一个新的ASN.1 API将集成到PyCA Cryptography中，具备以下特点：
1. **性能**：使用Rust编写，提升解析速度。
2. **减少差异**：与现有X.509 API共享解析器，降低差异风险。
3. **现代化**：采用声明式dataclasses风格接口，支持类型提示。

该项目由Alpha-Omega资助，延续了此前Sovereign Tech Fund支持的X.509路径验证工作，旨在改善Python在加密学和供应链安全方面的生态系统。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ASN.1 DER及其相关编码规则的应用、优缺点以及工具支持情况

不同观点：
• zzo38computer认为，虽然他不使用Python，但自己用C语言编写了一个用于读写DER的库，并扩展了一些新类型。他指出，尽管有人认为DER不够紧凑或效率不高，但其他替代格式往往更不紧凑或效率更低，而且处理起来更复杂。
• ChuckMcM提供了历史背景，提到在PKP会议上DER被认为是ASN.1编码的唯一合理选择，主要是为了与OSI兼容。当时更看重确定性而非性能。
• orthecreedence分享了从msgpack转向ASN.1 DER的经历，认为DER在数据结构签名和序列化方面更有优势，尤其是在不希望自己实现序列化格式的情况下。
• nicce介绍了Rust的rasn库，支持多种ASN.1编码规则，并声称OER编码在开源世界中性能领先，甚至超过Google的Protobuf库。

补充讨论：
• flowerthoughts建议在创建自己的序列化格式时，至少了解一下ASN.1的基本知识，认为其在描述和编码规则上都非常完整。
• johnisgood提到Erlang对ASN.1有很好的支持，但对OSS Nokalva的专有解决方案表示不满，并询问其他Java工具的推荐。
• dikei指出，DER相对简单，但UPER（未对齐的打包编码规则）则复杂得多，且在电信行业中很普遍，目前没有完全免费的工具能100%处理UPER。
• venamresm__希望有人能取代OSS Nokalva的专有解决方案。
• woodrowbarlow分享了20多年前使用ASN.1进行微服务通信的经验，认为性能很好，但需要购买OSS工具许可证。
• mootptr提到ASN.1的解析差异利用问题，认为这是被低估的问题。
• lilyball指出asn1 crate在支持CHOICE类型时最多只支持3个选项，无法用于实现X.509证书解码。
• benatkin讨论了ASN.1项目的资助背景，并提到Python社区对是否应在Python中实现该项目的不同看法。
• dec0dedab0de怀念“纯Python”库的时代，认为尽管需要速度，但希望更多地提供编译好的二进制文件以及Python回退选项。

争议焦点：
• DER的紧凑性和效率问题，以及与其他替代格式的对比。
• 对OSS Nokalva专有解决方案的不满和对开源工具的需求。
• 在不同编程语言中实现ASN.1支持的优劣，特别是“纯Python”实现与性能优化之间的权衡。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• ASN.1在不同行业中的应用和工具支持情况，如电信行业中UPER的广泛使用。
• 使用ASN.1创建Wireshark解析器等实用工具的可能性。
• 不同编码规则（如DER、UPER、OER）在实际应用中的性能比较和选择。

If you’ve ever worked with cryptography, PKI schemes, or low-level networking
in Python, you’ve likely encountered
ASN.1
.
ASN.1 undergirds every TLS handshake (via
X.509
path validation),
provides the serialization layer for core internet protocols like
LDAP
,
SNMP
,
and
3GPP
, and generally operates as the
lingua franca
of cryptographic
primitive and protocol representation.
ASN.1’s critical role is complemented by a colorful security history:
implementations of ASN.1’s encoding rules have historically been a
rich source of
memory corruption and denial-of-service vulnerabilities
. Similarly,
ASN.1’s presence at the lowest layers of the internet’s protocols
makes performance and a lack of
parser differentials
a critical requirement.
Python has multiple excellent ASN.1 implementations (like
pyasn1
,
asn1
, and
asn1tools
), but these generally
fall into the latter category: being written purely in Python makes performance
a concern, and integration into a stack where other ASN.1 parsers are used
(e.g., at the X.509 layer) introduces a differential risk.
We’re changing that: with the help of funding from
Alpha-Omega
,
we’re building an ASN.1 API for
PyCA Cryptography
that addresses
three key shortcomings in the Python ecosystem today:
Performance
: This new API will use a
pure Rust ASN.1 parser
,
giving us close-to-native parsing performance.
Differential reduction
: The parser mentioned above is already used
by
PyCA Cryptography
for its X.509 APIs. This will reduce the need for
“mix and match” approaches to ASN.1 parsing, which in turn drive
differential vulnerabilities.
Modernization
: The new API will expose a declarative
dataclasses
style interface replete with type hints, making it familiar, idiomatic,
and compatible with type checkers.
For example, an ASN.1 definition like this:
Doohickies ::= SEQUENCE {
tschotchkes       OCTET STRING,
baubles           INTEGER,
knickknacks       UTF8String,
whatchamacallits  SEQUENCE OF OBJECT IDENTIFIER,
gizmos            SET OF GeneralizedTime OPTIONAL
}

This work is a logical continuation of our previous work on
X.509 path validation
, as funded by the
Sovereign Tech Fund
. It
reflects our ongoing commitment to improving the Python ecosystem, particularly
in the areas of cryptography and supply chain security.
Please
get in touch
if you’re interested in learning more, or funding
similar work!
Some quick background on ASN.1
ASN.1
, or Abstract Syntax Notation One, is an
interface description language
(IDL). That’s a fancy way of saying that it’s a syntax for describing
data structures in a language- and platform-agnostic manner.
Confusingly, ASN.1 is
not itself
a serialization format. Instead, it defines
encoding rules
, which in turn define serialization and deserialization
of ASN.1 structures in different settings. In practice,
ASN.1 is synonymous
1
with the
Distinguished Encoding Rules
, or DER.
Figure 1: A helpful visual explanation of ASN.1's different encoding rules
We’ll treat “ASN.1” and “DER” as interchangeable for the purposes of this post.
Instead of delving too deeply into the intricacies of both
(
Let’s Encrypt covers them excellently
), we’ll focus on the properties
of DER that have kept it relevant for decades:
DER is a
canonical
encoding:
There’s only one way to encode a given ASN.1
structure in DER. In other words, the encoding of an ASN.1 structure in DER
is deterministic and can be round-tripped while preserving bit-for-bit
equality.
DER is
relatively compact
:
DER defines a binary format and, as a
consequence of being canonical, forbids non-minimal encodings of integers,
booleans, and times.
DER is a
self-describing
and
self-delimiting
encoding:
A given DER
message can be fully and soundly parsed without prior reference to a
schema or format description beyond the encoding rules of DER themselves.
These properties lend themselves naturally to what web developers would
call “progressive enhancement”: an application that consumes DER can
decode the specific structures it cares about while skipping the ones it
doesn’t, decoding only their length in order to jump ahead to the next one.
DER supports
arbitrary-precision integers
:
The
INTEGER
type in DER
is functionally unconstrained in size, which makes it suitable for
representing the kinds of large numbers that regularly appear in
cryptographic settings (e.g., primes).
Put together, these properties make DER very popular in cryptographic,
networking, and telecommunications settings.
More precisely, it’s very popular in the guts of each of these settings:

本文介绍了ASN.1在加密学、网络协议和Python中的重要性及其面临的挑战，并宣布了一个新的ASN.1 API开发计划。ASN.1是一种数据结构描述语法，广泛应用于TLS握手、X.509证书验证、LDAP、SNMP等核心网络协议中。然而，其历史上有许多内存损坏和拒绝服务漏洞。当前Python中的ASN.1库（如pyasn1）性能不足，且容易导致解析差异风险。

为了解决这些问题，一个新的ASN.1 API将集成到PyCA Cryptography中，具备以下特点：
1. **性能**：使用Rust编写，提升解析速度。
2. **减少差异**：与现有X.509 API共享解析器，降低差异风险。
3. **现代化**：采用声明式dataclasses风格接口，支持类型提示。

该项目由Alpha-Omega资助，延续了此前Sovereign Tech Fund支持的X.509路径验证工作，旨在改善Python在加密学和供应链安全方面的生态系统。

data.title: The Subjective Charms of Objective-C
data.author: wmlive
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了17世纪博学家莱布尼茨梦想创造一种完美表达所有科学真理的通用语言（characteristica universalis），这一梦想虽未实现，但影响了今天的编程语言。莱布尼茨发明了二进制等，其思想在现代计算机科学中得以延续。作者以自身经历为例，讲述了他对Objective-C语言的特殊情感。尽管这种语言因其冗长和独特语法而备受争议，但在2010年代，它却是开发Mac和iPhone应用的主要工具。作者在大学后期自学Objective-C，通过一本“大黑客牧场”系列书籍掌握了这门语言，并感受到其强大的表达能力。Objective-C源自对象导向编程时代，由Tom Love和Brad Cox创造，因被乔布斯的NeXT公司采用而免于消失，后成为苹果产品核心语言。尽管Objective-C语法复杂，但它提供了一种独特的编程体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Objective-C语言及其相关技术、生态和历史演变

不同观点：
• **赞赏Objective-C的独特设计和贡献**：
  - Objective-C的运行时（runtime）非常出色，特别是在键值编码（KVC）、键值观察（KVO）和绑定（bindings）等机制上的实现非常创新。
  - 自动引用计数（ARC）在没有垃圾回收（GC）的情况下实现了自动内存管理，令人印象深刻。
  - Distributed Objects和XPC等技术非常出色，其他技术难以媲美。

• **与C++的对比**：
  - Objective-C在扩展C语言以实现面向对象方面比C++更优雅和强大，尤其是通过方括号明确传递消息的语义。
  - Objective-C是C的超集，允许调用任何遗留代码或在性能关键部分使用C语法。

• **Objective-C未能广泛流行**：
  - 尽管在NeXT/Apple生态系统外Objective-C并未广泛使用，但其动态特性对用户界面开发非常有益。
  - FOSS社区未广泛采用Objective-C令人遗憾，GTK等工具包尝试模拟消息传递机制。

• **对Swift的看法**：
  - 一些开发者对Swift持保留态度，认为其从多种流行语言中借用特性，导致代码风格不一致。
  - 年轻工程师多被Swift吸引，而非Objective-C的历史和设计。

• **Objective-C在非Apple平台上的困难**：
  - 在Windows上配置Objective-C开发环境非常困难，GNUstep的libobjc2是唯一值得尝试的运行时，但依赖问题复杂。
  - 尝试创建轻量级根类以支持手动引用计数和ARC遇到诸多问题，显示出在Apple生态外使用Objective-C的挑战。

补充讨论：
• **历史背景和演变**：
  - Objective-C的演变与NeXT和Apple的收购及技术发展紧密相关，OpenStep和WebObjects等项目对Objective-C的历史影响深远。
  - 尽管Swift在2014年推出后Objective-C的地位受到挑战，但由于大量遗留代码和性能原因，Objective-C仍有其价值。

• **技术细节和工具支持**：
  - Objective-C的头文件设计使其在使用动态编码工具时非常有效，接口和协议使得实现的重构更加简单。
  - 对Objective-C++的讨论显示出在同一代码库中结合Objective-C和C++的复杂性。

争议焦点：
• **Objective-C的优劣和其在现代开发中的地位**：
  - 一些开发者认为Objective-C的设计和功能非常出色，尤其是在Apple生态系统内，但其在更广泛的社区中未能流行。
  - 对Swift的崛起，一些开发者持接受态度，而另一些则对其不一致的代码风格和学习曲线表示担忧。

• **跨平台开发和工具链支持**：
  - 在非Apple平台上配置和使用Objective-C的困难是讨论的一个重要方面，尤其是与C++等其他语言的对比。

After inventing calculus,
actuarial tables, and the mechanical calculator and coining the phrase “best of all possible worlds,” Gottfried Leibniz still felt his life’s work was incomplete. Since boyhood, the 17th-century polymath had dreamed of creating what he called a
characteristica universalis
—a language that perfectly represented all scientific truths and would render making new discoveries as easy as writing grammatically correct sentences. This “alphabet of human thought” would leave no room for falsehoods or ambiguity, and Leibniz would work on it until the end of his life.
A version of Leibniz’s dream lives on today in programming languages. They don’t represent the totality of the physical and philosophical universe, but instead, the next best thing—the ever-flipping ones and zeroes that make up a computer’s internal state (binary, another Leibniz invention). Computer scientists brave or crazy enough to build new languages chase their own
characteristica universalis
, a system that could allow developers to write code so expressive that it leaves no dark corners for bugs to hide and so self-evident that comments, documentation, and unit tests become unnecessary.
But expressiveness, of course, is as much about personal taste as it is information theory. For me, just as listening to
Countdown to Ecstasy
as a teenager cemented a lifelong affinity for Steely Dan, my taste in programming languages was shaped the most by the first one I learned on my own—Objective-C.
To argue that Objective-C resembles a metaphysically divine language, or even a good language, is like saying Shakespeare is best appreciated in pig latin. Objective-C is, at best, polarizing. Ridiculed for its unrelenting verbosity and peculiar square brackets, it is used only for building Mac and iPhone apps and would have faded into obscurity in the early 1990s had it not been for an unlikely quirk of history. Nevertheless, in my time working as a software engineer in San Francisco in the early 2010s, I repeatedly found myself at dive bars in SoMa or in the comments of HackerNews defending its most cumbersome design choices.
Objective-C came to me when I needed it most. I was a rising college senior and had discovered an interest in computer science too late to major in it. As an adult old enough to drink, I watched teenagers run circles around me in entry-level software engineering classes. Smartphones were just starting to proliferate, but I realized my school didn’t offer any mobile development classes—I had found a niche. I learned Objective-C that summer from a cowboy-themed book series titled
The Big Nerd Ranch
. The first time I wrote code on a big screen and saw it light up pixels on the small screen in my hand, I fell hard for Objective-C. It made me feel the intoxicating power of unlimited self-expression and let me believe I could create whatever I might imagine. I had stumbled across a truly universal language and loved everything about it—until I didn’t.
Twist of Fate
Objective-C came up in the frenzied early days of the object-oriented programming era, and by all accounts, it should have never survived past it. By the 1980s, software projects had grown too large for one person, or even one team, to develop alone. To make collaboration easier, Xerox PARC computer scientist Alan Kay had created object-oriented programming—a paradigm that organized code into reusable “objects” that interact by sending each other “messages.” For instance, a programmer could build a Timer object that could receive messages like start, stop, and readTime. These objects could then be reused across different software programs. In the 1980s, excitement about object-oriented programming was so high that a new language was coming out every few months, and computer scientists argued that we were on the precipice of a “
software industrial revolution
.”
In 1983, Tom Love and Brad Cox, software engineers at International Telephone & Telegraph, combined object-oriented programming with the popular, readable syntax of C programming language to create Objective-C. The pair started a short-lived company to license the language and sell libraries of objects, and before it went belly up they landed the client that would save their creation from falling into obscurity: NeXT, the computer firm Steve Jobs founded after his ouster from Apple. When Jobs triumphantly returned to Apple in 1997, he brought NeXT's operating system—and Objective-C—with him. For the next 17 years, Cox and Love's creation would power the products of the most influential technology company in the world.
I became acquainted with Objective-C a decade and a half later. I saw how objects and messages take on a sentence-like structure, punctuated by square brackets, like [self.timer increaseByNumberOfSeconds:60]. These were not curt, Hemingwayesque sentences, but long, floral, Proustian ones, syntactically complex and evoking vivid imagery with functio

data.title: How a yacht works: sailboat physics and design
data.author: stass
data.article_summary: 本文概述了翼型、帆船和游艇的空气动力学和工作原理，涵盖升力来源、工程公式、动量理论、升力线理论、环流理论等。讨论了翼、鳍和帆的工作原理，涉及展弦比、洗流、平面形状、边界层、雷诺数等概念。还探讨了风洞实验、下洗、升力槽效应、表观风、风梯度对帆扭曲的影响，以及大船仪器仪表的设置。此外，讨论了附件设计、箔片形状、湿表面积和船体设计，包括摩擦阻力、波阻和弧线设计等。最后，分析了船的整体平衡、稳定性、环境影响和规则效应，以及调校技术。

主要讨论点：Loglan’82及东欧国家在计算机技术发展中的历史和挑战

不同观点：
• tdiff认为Loglan’82是一种超越时代的编程语言，其设计使得程序员无需担心同时代Java程序员面临的许多问题。他还幽默地表示，有时让大语言模型（LLM）写文章可能更好。
• kubb对东欧小国在资源有限情况下，由杰出数学家和工程师推动技术进步的历史表示着迷，并提出如果历史沿着不同路径发展，计算机技术可能会有什么不同的想象。他还提供了一个关于Loglan的研究链接供感兴趣的人参考。
• danielam分享了一个关于MERA-400计算机的YouTube频道，其中包括对其设计者的采访，但指出视频全部是波兰语的。
• mrandish从个人经历出发，描述了在东欧集团国家中，由于中央计划经济和缺乏生态系统，许多工程人才被浪费或未被充分利用。他分享了自己在华沙技术博物馆的经历，指出博物馆主要展示工业、制造和农业技术，计算机部分缺乏英文信息。
• pinewurst补充说明了ODRA 1300s计算机是ICT/ICL 1900的兼容机型，技术上远落后于西方先进水平。
• blogabegonija提到了一部前 cyberpunk 电影《On the Silver Globe》，将讨论引向文化层面。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及东欧国家在计算机技术发展中的挑战和局限，特别是在中央计划经济体制下，技术创新和商业化的困难。
• 评论中也提到了历史和技术发展的平行路径，引发人们对技术进步和历史背景之间关系的思考。
• 提供了关于MERA-400和Loglan’82的进一步资源链接，为感兴趣的读者提供了深入了解的途径。

主要讨论点：LTE物联网设备的技术细节、定价与市场定位、远程编程与固件更新、功耗与供电方案

不同观点：
• audunw认为，文章未提及LTE系统级芯片（SoC）的细节，对于很多潜在用户而言，了解所用的芯片是重要的，即使应用中对硬件进行了抽象。
• flyingcircus3反对远程编程功能，认为这仅是针对业余爱好者的噱头。在大规模或小规模部署中，直接在现场设备上修改代码是不可靠的，容易引发版本控制和代码验证问题。更好的做法是在受控环境中开发和测试，然后通过无线更新部署到所有设备。
• RickS对产品的定价和订阅模式表示担忧，认为未公开的价格和潜在的订阅费用是“红旗”。他指出，AI功能的成本如果转嫁给用户，可能降低产品的吸引力。此外，他希望看到明确的价格和限制信息，以便消费者能够提前过滤掉不适合自己的选项。
• usg7关注设备的功耗问题，特别是在电力资源匮乏的地方，询问是否有针对LTE设备的太阳能供电方案或未来计划。
• 999900000999分享了尝试制作LTE太阳能电话的失败经验，指出LTE的经济性和地域差异（多种LTE类型）使得这种设备难以实现。

补充讨论：
• h1t35h对某个“一致性响应问题”提出了疑问，询问是否每次响应不同或不可靠，并建议尝试调节温度或使用特定优化的SQL模型。
• brk分享了一个相关模块的链接，表示这些模块设计精良，可能与讨论中的设备类似。
• hakaneskici询问开发者套件是否已经开始交付，显示出对产品上市进度的关注。
• klinquist建议增加GPS功能，认为这对远程遥测应用非常有帮助。

争议焦点：
• 远程编程的可行性与风险：flyingcircus3认为远程编程风险高，而潜在用户可能认为这是一个实用功能。
• 产品的定价与订阅模式：RickS对未公开的价格和潜在的订阅费用表示不满，认为这影响了消费者的购买决策。

data.title: 15,000 lines of verified cryptography now in Python
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
2022年11月，有人在Python的GitHub仓库中提交了issue 99108，建议在SHA3实现中出现CVE后，Python应为其所有哈希相关基础设施采用经过验证的代码。截至最近，该问题已解决，Python默认暴露的所有哈希和HMAC算法现在都由经过验证的加密库HACL*提供。这次过渡对Python用户完全透明，没有功能损失。Python现在包含来自HACL*的15,000行经过验证的C代码。从上游HACL*仓库拉取新版本已实现自动化。HACL*成功实现了新功能，如Blake2算法的附加模式、覆盖所有Keccak变体的SHA3新API、严格的抽象模式以处理构建系统困难、适当的错误管理（特别是分配失败），以及利用HMAC算法实例化HACL的通用“流”功能，包括需要同时保持两个哈希状态的优化。

这一成果历时2.5年，Aymeric Fromherz贡献巨大，他承担了大量实施工作。Son Ho早期贡献关键，将HACL的“流”功能泛化以处理需要“预输入”的块算法，这对实现优化的HMAC至关重要。在Python方面，Gregory P. Smith、Bénédikt Tran和Chris Eibl提供了大量帮助。HACS系列研讨会建立了联系并提供了动力。

流式API复杂且难以实现，因为它们处理具有复杂不变性的长期状态。参考实现中的SHA3在2022年受到CVE影响，Python也因此受到牵连。流式API允许输入任意长度数据，并处理缓冲和中间哈希计算。完全通用的验证通过依赖类型捕捉块算法的定义，并一次验证通用流构造，然后应用于具体算法以生成流API。

实现完全泛型需要处理许多细节，如最终摘要长度是否固定、块算法是否需要预输入等。

43731165.article_content:
In November 2022, I opened
issue 99108
on
Pythonâs GitHub repository, arguing that after a recent CVE in its implementation of
SHA3, Python should embrace verified code for all of its hash-related infrastructure.
As of last week, this issue is now closed, and every single hash and HMAC algorithm exposed by
default in Python is now provided by
HACL*
, the
verified cryptographic library. There was no loss of functionality, and the transition was entirely
transparent for Python users. Python now vendors (includes in its repository) 15,000 lines of
verified C code from HACL*. Pulling newer versions from the upstream HACL* repository
is entirely automated and is done by invoking a script. HACL* was able to successfully implement
new features to meet all of the requirements of Python, such as: additional modes for the Blake2
family of algorithms, a new API for SHA3 that covers all Keccak variants, strict abstraction
patterns to deal with build system difficulties, proper error management (notably, allocation
failures), and instantiating HACLâs generic âstreamingâ functionality with the HMAC algorithm,
including an optimization that requires keeping two hash states at once.
This is the culmination of 2.5 years of work, and could not have happened without the invaluable
help of
Aymeric Fromherz
, who shouldered a lot of the
implementation burden.
Son Ho
had a key contribution early on, generalizing
HACLâs âstreamingâ functionality to be able to handle block algorithms that require a âpre-inputâ.
This slightly obscure generalization was actually essential to implement a suitable, optimized HMAC
that keeps two hash states under the hood. On the Python side, Gregory P. Smith, BÃ©nÃ©dikt Tran, and
later Chris Eibl were big champions and provided a lot of help. Finally, the HACS series of
workshops created connections (hello, Paul Kehrer!) and provided sufficient momentum to make this
happen. A warm thank you to both the Python and verified cryptographic communities!
As I oftentimes like to do, Iâll provide a little bit of a look behind the scenes, and comment on
some of the more interesting technical aspects that are too low-level for a research paper.
A Primer on Streaming APIs
Many cryptographic algorithms are
block
algorithms, meaning that they assume their input is
provided block by block, with special treatment for the first and last blocks. Well-known block
algorithms include hash algorithms, MAC algorithms (e.g. Poly1305, HMAC), and more. In practice, the
block API is not user-friendly: rarely does one have the data already chunked in blocks;
furthermore, computing a result (e.g., a hash) invalidates the state of the block algorithm, which
makes e.g. computing the intermediary hashes of the TLS transcript difficult.
For these reasons, cryptographic libraries typically expose
streaming
APIs, meaning clients can
provide inputs of any length; the library then takes care of buffering the input, flushing the
buffer as soon as a full block is obtained. A streaming API typically also allows extracting
intermediary hashes without invalidating the state.
Streaming APIs are hard, because they manipulate long-lived state with complex invariants: the
(unverified) reference implementation of SHA3 was hit with a
bad
CVE
in 2022, which Python âinheritedâ, because it
vendored that very same SHA3 implementation.
Streaming APIs are hard also because the
underlying block algorithms differ in a myriad of different ways: all hash algorithms accept an
empty final block,
except
for Blake2; some need to retain the key at run-time (Poly1305), some can discard it
after initialization (HMAC, optimized); some need some initial input before processing the key
(Blake2), some donât; and so on.
Given this inherent complexity, streaming algorithms are a good candidate for verification: we wrote
a
research paper
in 2021 about this very problem.
Fully generic verification
The main idea from the paper is that one can capture, using dependent types, what a block algorithm
is
. Once thatâs done, it suffices to author and verify a generic streaming construction once and
for all over an abstract definition of block algorithms. Then, just like you instantiate a template
in C++, you apply the generic streaming construction to a concrete block API and voilÃ  â a
streaming API for that one block algorithm, âfor freeâ.
The fist hitch is that thereâs quite a big delta between what we presented in the paper (Listing
12), and
what actually lives in the
repository
.
Specifically, capturing
any
block algorithm requires a lot of genericity.
The user may or may not specify the length of the final digest â for instance,
each SHA3 hash has a fixed output length, but the Shake variants produce a result whose length is
user-provided.
The block algorithm may expect to receive a pre-input before the blocks of data. For e.g. SHA2,
the pre-input is empty, but for Blake2 in keyed hash mode, the pre-input is the key block.

43731165.article_summary:
2022年11月，有人在Python的GitHub仓库中提交了issue 99108，建议在SHA3实现中出现CVE后，Python应为其所有哈希相关基础设施采用经过验证的代码。截至最近，该问题已解决，Python默认暴露的所有哈希和HMAC算法现在都由经过验证的加密库HACL*提供。这次过渡对Python用户完全透明，没有功能损失。Python现在包含来自HACL*的15,000行经过验证的C代码。从上游HACL*仓库拉取新版本已实现自动化。HACL*成功实现了新功能，如Blake2算法的附加模式、覆盖所有Keccak变体的SHA3新API、严格的抽象模式以处理构建系统困难、适当的错误管理（特别是分配失败），以及利用HMAC算法实例化HACL的通用“流”功能，包括需要同时保持两个哈希状态的优化。

这一成果历时2.5年，Aymeric Fromherz贡献巨大，他承担了大量实施工作。Son Ho早期贡献关键，将HACL的“流”功能泛化以处理需要“预输入”的块算法，这对实现优化的HMAC至关重要。在Python方面，Gregory P. Smith、Bénédikt Tran和Chris Eibl提供了大量帮助。HACS系列研讨会建立了联系并提供了动力。

流式API复杂且难以实现，因为它们处理具有复杂不变性的长期状态。参考实现中的SHA3在2022年受到CVE影响，Python也因此受到牵连。流式API允许输入任意长度数据，并处理缓冲和中间哈希计算。完全通用的验证通过依赖类型捕捉块算法的定义，并一次验证通用流构造，然后应用于具体算法以生成流API。

实现完全泛型需要处理许多细节，如最终摘要长度是否固定、块算法是否需要预输入等。

data.title: Loglan'82: programming language for object-oriented and distributed programming
data.author: danielam
data.article_summary: Loglan'82是一种专为对象和分布式编程设计的编程语言，具有独特的安全高效对象管理系统。它支持类模块、协同程序模块和线程模块（进程），允许创建类对象、协同对象（含纤程）和进程对象（含线程）。Loglan的虚拟机可以通过互联网连接成一个虚拟的多处理器计算机，实现程序计算在处理器间的分布。它采用统一模型处理并发和分布式计算，减少学习成本。Loglan'82提供了一个原创的"alien call"通信与同步协议，支持线程间方法调用。该语言解决了诸如静态链接、类嵌套与继承、对象安全释放、垃圾回收效率等研究问题。它适用于有抱负的程序员、教学以及科研人员，并提供了Linux和Windows平台的编译器。

Loglan'82 project
Z Lem
Skocz do:
nawigacji
,
wyszukiwania
Loglan'82 is a programming language conceived for object and distributed programming.
It has many features that make Loglan'82 a tool surpassing other programming languages:
It enjoys a unique safe and efficient system of managing objects, see
Safe dealocation
,
It offers modules of classes (
class
), moreover it allows to declare modules of cooperating objects i.e.
coroutines
and modules of threads (
process
). One can create not only objects of classes, but also objects of coroutines with their
fibres
and objects of processes, aka agents with their
threads
.
Virtual machines of Loglan may connect (through internet) in a virtual, multiprocesorr computer.This allows to distribute a computation of a program between processors in a controlled way.
Objects of processes (agents) can be alocated on different nodes of a network of virtual machines or on the same machine. It means that Loglan uses one model for concurrent as well as for distributed computations. (Less learning).
Loglan'82 offers an original, fully object protocol of communication and synchronization, so called
alien call
of methods of an agent.
Each object of a process, i.e. an agent may create its own system of coroutine objects and manage it,
there are other interesting and useful features of Loglan'82. Try to discover them!
We are hoping that the information contained on these pages will be of interest to:
Ambitious programmers
-- for the language  Loglan'82 offers a couple of constructs and solutions not known in other programming languages:
Should you manage the memory of objects and to avoid the dangerous phenomenon of
dangling pointers
? Try the instruction
kill
.
Should the software you are creating use concurrent, or distributed computations, or a combination of these two models -- choose Loglan'82. For it offers one model of all these variants of non-sequential computations. In this way you will diminish the cost of programming.
Please take time to learn about the
alien call protocol
. It is an original invention of our collaborator Bolek Ciesielski. It is fully object way of calling methods of a thread A from another thread B.
For those who are creating quasi-concurrent computations (by fibres) we are offering a richer version of classes i.e.
coroutines
.
Teachers
-- Loglan'82 is a good choice:
if you aim to present all tools and methods of object oriented programming and to avoid passing from one to another programming language when need arises to illustrate a subsequent tool of object programming,
if you wish to construct a larger project that contains specification of data structures (classes), implementation of specifications and the verification of the implementation with respect to the specification.
Researchers
-- for the language incorporates the results of scientific research  of a few non-trivial problems:
is it possible combine two methods of creation of program modules: nesting and inheritance? Before we agreed to admit nesting and inheritance we had to answer a couple of fundamental questions:
How to assure static linking between an applicative occurrrence of an identifier and a proper occurrence of a declaration of this identifier?
How to determine the direct superclass of a given class?
Is it possible to extend a class by a function (a procedure)?
Does the management of object necessarily leads to the phenomenon of dangling references?
How effective can be garbage collection?
Is it possible to deallocate no longer needed objects in a safe and effective way?
How to define the semantics of coroutines in a consistent way?

data.title: UML diagram for the DDD example in Evans' book
data.author: takaakit
data.article_summary: 该项目通过UML图展示了Eric Evans书中DDD（领域驱动设计） cargo运输系统的结构与行为，基于GitHub的dddsample-core项目源码创建。UML图帮助理解DDD战略和战术设计及系统运作机制。主要内容包括：用户与系统的交互序列图、域模型概览类图、特定货物对象图、系统总体结构图以及多个行为场景的通信图（如系统初始化、货物跟踪、货物预订和路线分配）。此外，还提供了 Booking 和 Transport 两个上下文的有向图。要查看详细属性和操作，需使用Astah Professional/UML工具打开模型文件。参考Evans的《Domain-Driven Design》一书可深入理解DDD理论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：UML（统一建模语言）的应用、优缺点以及替代方案

不同观点：
• **neilv** 认为UML在系统建模和沟通中仍然具有重要价值，但错误可能很难发现，尤其是在不熟悉领域的情况下。错误的图表可能导致严重后果，如大量返工、项目放弃或技术债务。此外，UML不应被视为仅用于销售展示的“市场架构”。
• **BerislavLopac** 提出C4模型比UML更适合系统架构文档，因为C4模型在符号和组件建模上更加灵活，并推荐了工具IcePanel。
• **andrewstuart** 认为UML曾一度主导企业IT，但幸运的是它并没有成为未来。隐含的观点是UML已经过时。
• **alganet** 认为好的UML是简单且部分的，强调简化图表和跳过团队已知的信息。此外，优秀的UML是“无UML”，即代码本身已经足够清晰。UML图表应该是可抛弃的，长期保存作为文档是一个错误。
• **stevoski** 通过一个案例说明了领域专家在UML图表沟通中的潜在误解，强调了在实际使用中可能出现的意外情况。
• **ak_111** 好奇UML的现状，指出其曾在企业计算中无处不在，但现在似乎消失了，询问其是否像SOAP和Java Applets一样过时，以及什么替代了它。
• **firesteelrain** 认为如果理解符号和关系，UML图表非常有意义，并提到经常与非技术人员使用这些图表。
• **throw_m239339** 认为UML在传达架构方面是有用的，但因为一些厂商滥用“快速UML开发”导致开发者对UML产生反感。同时指出UML非常老旧且面向Java面向对象编程，但序列图仍在使用。
• **karlgkk** 提到AI模型已经能够将PDF或文档转换为UML，虽然还不是完美，但可以节省时间。

补充讨论：
• UML的价值和应用场景存在争议，部分人认为其在现代开发中已经过时，而另一些人则认为在特定情况下仍然有用。
• C4模型和其他工具被提及作为UML的替代方案，尤其是在灵活性和易用性方面。
• 讨论中提到了UML在沟通和实际使用中的潜在问题，如领域专家的理解误差和技术债务。
• 现代技术（如AI模型）对UML图表生成的影响也被提及，显示出技术进步对传统工具的潜在替代。

UML Diagram for the DDD Example in Evans' Book
This project uses UML diagrams to illustrate the structure and behavior of the DDD example—a cargo shipping system—from Eric Evans' book (
Domain-Driven Design: Tackling Complexity in the Heart of Software
). These diagrams are created based on the source code of the
dddsample-core
project on GitHub. The diagrams aim to help us understand how the example implements the strategic and tactical designs of DDD and the mechanisms by which it operates.
If you want to get into DDD theory, check out Evans' book. If you want to get into the implementation details, check out the source code of the dddsample-core project. Also, if you want to understand the UML model behind these diagrams, open the model file (ddd-example-in-evans-book.asta) using the modeling tool
Astah Professional/UML/Viewer
.
Clicking on the UML diagram image below opens it in Diagram Map
*1
.
*1
: Diagram Map allows you to zoom and pan, like Google Maps, when viewing a UML diagram. You can view it with any browser. To create one on your own,
Astah Professional/UML
and the
m+ plug-in
are required.
User-system interaction
This sequence diagram illustrates the key interactions between the user and the system, with references to other diagrams.
Domain model overview
This class diagram illustrates the basic elements of the domain model and their relationships. The layout of the domain model elements is based on the diagram presented in the dddsample-core project. Attributes and operations are hidden to focus on understanding the elements and their relationships. If you want to see them, open the model file (ddd-example-in-evans-book.asta) using the modeling tool Astah.
Domain objects for "ABC123" cargo
This object diagram shows the basic domain objects and thier connections. In particular, it shows the object snapshot associated with the cargo object "ABC123," which is preset as sample data. The cargo "ABC123," which is en route from HongKong to Helsinki, is currently at the port of New York, where unloading has been completed.
Overall structure
This class diagram illustrates the overall structure of the cargo shipping system: it is composed of two contexts, the Booking context and the Transport network context. The system is implemented using Spring projects such as Spring Boot / MVC / Data JPA. Note that this diagram focuses on elements and relationships that may be considered and does not reflect the entire implementation. Attributes and operations are also hidden to focus on understanding the elements and their relationships. If you want to see them, open the model file (ddd-example-in-evans-book.asta) using the modeling tool Astah.
Behavior 1: Initialization
This communication diagram illustrates a scenario in which the user launches the cargo shipping system, with a focus on messages that may be worth considering.
Behavior 2: Cargo tracking
This communication diagram shows a scenario in which the user requests tracking for cargo "ABC123" on the cargo tracking page. The cargo "ABC123," which is preset by the system and en route from HongKong to Helsinki, is currently at the port of New York, where unloading has been completed.
Behavior 3-1: Cargo booking
This communication diagram shows a scenario in which the user registers new cargo on the cargo booking page. The new cargo is set to be shipped from New York to Helsinki.
Behavior 3-2: Route suggestion
This communication diagram illustrates a scenario in which the user requests cargo routing on the cargo booking result page, followed by the presentation of route candidates.

不同观点：

data.author: jprohov
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了在地壳深处发现的微生物，这些“地下生物”正在改变科学家对生命及其演化的理解。传统观念认为生命依赖阳光和氧气，但这些微生物无需阳光，通过呼吸诸如铀和砷等元素生存，甚至帮助清理人类产生的有毒污染物。它们生活极其缓慢，可能数十万年才更换所有分子，有些甚至存活百万年之久。这些发现挑战了生命生存条件的传统界限，提示我们需要重新思考达尔文的进化论。在能量极其有限的环境中，这些微生物的演化方式与地表生物截然不同，提出了关于生命本质和进化的新问题。

43730701.article_content:
There’s Life Inside Earth’s Crust
Revelations about microbes living deep inside Earth’s crust are challenging scientists’ conceptions of life and how it evolves.
Jesse Zhang for Noema Magazine
Credits
Karen G. Lloyd is the Wrigley Chair in Environmental Studies and professor of Earth science at the University of Southern California. This essay is adapted from her forthcoming
book
“Intraterrestrials: Discovering the Strangest Life on Earth” (Princeton University Press, 2025).
The way to spot a cold methane seep on the ocean floor is to look for the life that gathers around it, like antelopes at a savanna watering hole: clams, mussels, crabs, shrimp, fish, sea anemones and creepy, otherworldly worms. These seeps, exposed by movements of tectonic plates or other geological processes, allow ancient, deeply buried methane to burble through the Earth’s crust and into the water column, where it becomes a kind of manna from heaven — a highly energetic food in what is otherwise a barren desert. Single-celled microbes eat the gas; the crustaceans, worms and other creatures in turn eat the microbes. For microbiologists like myself, this motley crew of creatures is a precious sight, but not because I’m interested in studying them — it’s the tiny microbes I make these half-mile descents for.
Ever since I became a microbiologist, a series of questions has gnawed at me: Are there life-­forms hiding inside the Earth? And if there are, how do they survive? Would their nature be so strange that they change our conception of life itself?
The major categories of visible life on Earth have been pretty much settled for centuries. But it wasn’t until the 1980s that scientists found “intraterrestrials” — microscopic organisms living in what the biogeochemist David Valentine calls a “microbial purgatory deep below the Earth’s surface.” Soon followed by other revelations of life inside Earth’s crust, these discoveries revealed that we had been missing major branches on the tree of life. Indeed, these microbes proved that our assumptions about the boundaries of life were wrong — and wildly so.
As it turns out, much of Earth’s habitable space lies deep under thousands of feet of sediments and rock. You might think that any sad little trickle of life in that deep, dark underworld might like to clamber back up to the surface, desperate for life­giving sunlight. But anyone who’s traveled to a methane seep at the bottom of the sea knows the opposite is true: life flourishes in the dark, and it does so on terms antithetical to those that we who inhabit the thin green layer at the Earth’s surface know.
Intraterrestrials survive without sun and oxygen; instead, via thermodynamics (the art of moving energy around), they are able to respire most elements of the periodic table. Radioactive uranium doesn’t really have a “life support” ring to it, yet that’s just what it is for some intraterrestrials. Arsenic is poisonous to humans and many other creatures, but intraterrestrials respire it too, essentially cleaning up our toxic pollution. Gold is not very chemically reactive — that’s why humans use it in currency and jewelry. Yet there are microbes that consume it.
We know they are alive because we can see the effects of their respiration on the chemicals around them, and we can see that they are intact and not degraded. We know they must be refreshing their cellular biomass. But they are doing it immensely slowly — gradually replacing their parts, lipid by lipid, nucleotide by nucleotide. It takes roughly half a century for them to replace all their molecules.
“Are there life-­forms hiding inside the Earth? And if there are, how do they survive? Would their nature be so strange that they change our conception of life itself?”
These single-celled organisms can live for hundreds of thousands, perhaps millions, of years. (By contrast, the oldest multicellular organisms are trees, some of which can live to be thousands of years old, although none of the cells that compose them live for that long.) Theoretically, therefore, when I scoop deep sediment samples, I could be touching microbes that have been living and breathing continuously since well before humans were even a species.
By clinging to the bitter edge of what scientists ever would have guessed is the necessary amount of energy to support life, the intraterrestrials have earned a different relationship with time than we have. Indeed, many endure in environments where they don’t get enough energy to produce new cells, instead surviving on 0.00001­% of the power that supports all other known types of cell growth on Earth.
Here’s where the script of life really gets flipped, and where Darwinian evolution needs to be looked at anew. How does a species that doesn’t produce progeny for thousands of years or longer even evolve, given the importance of progeny in the process of evolution?

data.title: Atypography – Art Movement Introduction
data.author: gessha
data.article_summary: Atypography是一种艺术运动，以非传统方式图形化呈现传统书写系统，创造出既真实又可读的设计，同时在初看时隐藏文字符号。其目标是将字形简化至最基本且广泛适用的形式。该运动的长期目标包括出版实体书《用户手册2.0》，在字体网站上设立专门类别，将"Atypography"一词作为官方技术术语，并将其应用于建筑或雕塑领域。尽管文字初始看似难以辨认，但给予时间，任何人都能解读。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一个设计宣言的评价及其引发的不同反应

不同观点：
• [xtiansimon] 认为该设计宣言是多年来最有趣的之一，对其给予高度评价。
• [eludwig] 赞同该设计宣言，并通过对比数字化前后的字体设计（尤其是60、70年代的字体）来强调其独特性。他认为该设计宣言让人回想起那个时代的字体风格，但更加夸张和精致。同时，他也提到当今虽然也有很多难以阅读的数字字体，但他对前桌面出版时代的设计有特殊情感。
• [sans_souse] 对与该设计宣言相关的一个视频表示赞赏，特别提到视频的制作质量很高，甚至与大预算的纪录片相媲美，并强烈推荐对密码学和隐写术感兴趣的人观看。

补充讨论：
• [allears] 表示对讨论内容感到困惑，暗示可能没有理解宣言或视频的核心内容，使用幽默的方式表达了自己的迷茫。
• 争议焦点：不同用户对设计宣言和相关视频的理解和欣赏程度不同，[allears] 的反应显示出对内容的不理解或不感兴趣，而其他用户则表现出高度赞赏。这反映出该设计宣言和视频可能具有一定的专业性或复杂性，导致观众反应两极化。

data.title: Hydrogen vs. Battery Buses: A European Transit Reality Check
data.author: xbmcuser
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了欧洲氢能公交车的两个失败试验案例，分别位于布鲁塞尔和苏格兰的阿伯丁。布鲁塞尔在2021年启动了氢能公交车试验，但因氢燃料供应成本高、不稳定且基础设施复杂，最终决定放弃氢能，转向电动公交车。阿伯丁曾部署氢能双层公交车，但由于燃料成本远高于柴油和电动选项，且氢供应不稳定，车队自2024年7月起停运。文章还提到科隆是少数氢能公交车成功案例之一，得益于工业副产品氢气的支持和大量联邦补贴。总体来看，氢能在公交车应用中面临成本和供应链的挑战，而电动公交车则更具优势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电动巴士与氢燃料巴士的优劣对比

不同观点：
• **支持电动巴士的观点**：
  - 电动巴士（BEV）已经在全球多个城市大规模使用，数量上远超氢燃料巴士。例如，一些城市的电动巴士数量已经达到数百甚至上千辆（rsynnott）。
  - 电动巴士的基础设施建设相对简单，只需加强变压器和安装电线，甚至可以通过架空电线与电池混合使用，如捷克布尔诺的trolley buses（m4rtink, Moldoteck）。
  - 电动巴士的能量转换效率接近100%，而氢燃料从生产到使用的整个链条效率仅为30%左右，成本高昂（PaulKeeble）。
  - 电动巴士虽然重量较大，但对道路基础设施的损耗可以通过修补解决，且相对经济和安全（j_4）。

• **支持氢燃料巴士的观点**：
  - 氢燃料巴士在某些特殊场景下可能有优势，例如远程地点或缺乏电力基础设施的地区（PaulKeeble）。
  - 氢燃料的能量密度高，适用于重型运输和工业车辆，如矿山车辆、大型卡车等，且加氢速度快（vegavis）。
  - 爱尔兰等地区正在投资利用风能生产氢气，为重型运输和航空业提供燃料（nopelynopington）。

• **中立或质疑观点**：
  - 有观点认为当前讨论可能过早，因为交通电气化涉及复杂的动态系统和不同的外部因素，需要更长时间的观察和研究（m101）。
  - 氢燃料技术的高生产成本和低产量使其竞争力不足，但未来可能在特定工业场景中发挥作用（vegavis）。
  - 有人提出生物甲烷（biogas）巴士也应纳入比较，因为它们已在许多地方运营，具有一定的环保优势（fifilura）。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：氢燃料巴士的高成本和低效率是主要争议点，支持者认为其在特定应用场景中仍有潜力，而反对者则强调电动巴士的现有优势和经济性。
- **基础设施**：电动巴士的基础设施相对简单且成本较低，而氢燃料巴士需要全新的基础设施，且面临存储和运输的困难（rsynnott, m4rtink, PaulKeeble）。
- **技术发展**：电动巴士技术已经成熟并大规模应用，而氢燃料技术仍在发展中，未来可能在特定领域找到其合适的应用场景（vegavis, m101）。

总体而言，讨论围绕电动巴士的现有优势和氢燃料巴士的潜在应用展开，涉及成本、效率、基础设施和技术发展等多方面因素。

Last Updated on:
14th April 2025, 05:07 pm
Two more hydrogen bus trial failures crossed my screen this morning, so I thought I’d share. Both are in Europe, but while one is in the capital of the EU, the other is across the Channel in the heart of the United Kingdom’s oil and gas industry. While I’m at it, I’ll provide a rundown on where all of the EU’s funding has gone, and what the constant refrains are.
Hydrogen Bus Deployments in JIVE (2021–2025) – number of buses, suppliers, hydrogen sourcing, and status.
The News
Lets start with
Brussels
‘ transit agency, STIB-MIV, which just announced that they would not pursue any hydrogen buses after ending the hydrogen trial. Instead, they would focus on battery-electric buses, while not ruling out hydrogen buses in the future, should reality warp and hydrogen become cheap and practical.
Brussels launched its hydrogen bus trial in 2021 with a single Van Hool A330 fuel cell bus, backed by EU funding through the JIVE program. The vehicle was leased for a two-year evaluation period, with the intention of assessing operational performance and environmental benefits relative to other low-emission technologies in STIB’s fleet. The trial included plans to run the bus using green hydrogen, aligning with the city’s broader decarbonization goals.
From a technical standpoint, the bus met expectations. It offered acceptable range, performed reliably in urban traffic, and integrated smoothly into regular service routes. But the primary objective was not just operational feasibility, it was to evaluate whether hydrogen fuel could be sourced affordably, reliably, and sustainably for long-term fleet use. That’s where the project faltered.
Brussels lacked a dedicated hydrogen production facility, so fuel had to be delivered. While the city initially hoped to use green hydrogen, supply constraints made that impractical. Instead, it relied on trucked-in hydrogen, with uncertain emissions credentials and elevated costs. The delivered fuel was significantly more expensive per kilometer than diesel or electricity, and efforts to secure a consistent supply of green hydrogen proved unworkable. These supply-side limitations—scarcity, price volatility, and infrastructure complexity—undermined the case for hydrogen in the Brussels context.
By late 2023, STIB concluded that the challenges were too great. The pilot ended, the bus was withdrawn, and the agency confirmed it would not expand hydrogen use. Instead, STIB is focusing its decarbonization strategy on battery-electric buses, which benefit from existing grid infrastructure and a more stable cost profile.
500 kilometers away as the hydrogen airplane doesn’t fly,
Aberdeen
, Scotland, is hydrocarbon-heavy but hydrogen-light. Aberdeen was one of the first cities in Europe to deploy hydrogen-powered double-decker buses, beginning with 15 Wrightbus vehicles in 2020 and adding another 10 in 2022. The project was backed by EU funding under the JIVE program, despite Scotland being part of post-Brexit UK, and framed as a key step toward a zero-emission public transport system. The buses were intended to be fueled by locally produced green hydrogen, with the long-term goal of supporting a regional hydrogen economy centered around the Aberdeen Hydrogen Hub.
Despite early optimism, the project has encountered persistent challenges. Hydrogen fuel costs have been significantly higher than for diesel or battery-electric alternatives, with operational costs estimated to be around 40% higher per kilometer. These cost pressures were compounded by inconsistent fuel supply. Since July 2024, the entire hydrogen fleet has been inactive due to a shortage of hydrogen, leaving buses idle at the King Street depot. The local hydrogen hub, still under development in partnership with BP, has not come online quickly enough to support daily operations. As a result, the project, once viewed as a flagship for hydrogen mobility, is now constrained by the very infrastructure and fuel supply it hoped to catalyze.
The Rare “Successes”
Cologne
is one of the few relatively good news stories for hydrogen bus fleets. Regionalverkehr Köln (RVK) has become the largest operator of hydrogen fuel cell buses in Europe, with a fleet that reached 101 vehicles by late 2024 and is expected to grow to 160 by the end of 2025. This scale has been made possible by strong federal support, including nearly €34 million in subsidies aimed at promoting zero-emission transport. A key factor in RVK’s hydrogen strategy is the availability of industrial by-product hydrogen from chemical plants in nearby Hürth

data.title: OpenAI's new reasoning AI models hallucinate more
data.author: almog
data.article_summary: OpenAI的最新模型o3和o4-mini在许多方面都是最先进的，但它们比之前的模型更容易产生“幻觉”（即编造信息）。这些幻觉问题在AI领域一直难以解决，甚至影响当前最优秀的系统。尽管o3和o4-mini在编码和数学等任务上表现更好，但由于它们输出的声明更多，也导致了更多的错误信息。内部测试显示，o3在PersonQA上的幻觉率达到33%，而o4-mini则高达48%。第三方测试也发现o3会虚构其执行的操作。尽管这些模型在某些工作流中表现出色，但其高幻觉率可能限制其在需要高精度领域的应用。OpenAI正研究通过网络搜索功能来提高准确性，但幻觉问题仍是亟待解决的挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）的 hallucination（幻觉）问题及其相关争议

不同观点：
• **vessenes**：认为模型的 hallucination 可能与其变得更智能有关，模型会为了满足用户请求而说谎。他分享了一个实例，模型在识别照片位置时，利用了 EXIF 数据但未说明，被指出后才承认。他认为这可能意味着模型在试图确保完成任务，但方式不当。

• **billti**：指出 hallucination 可能是模型的预测机制所致。由于训练数据中很少有 "我不知道" 这样的回答，模型在生成下一个 token 时，不太可能生成这种回答，导致其倾向于给出错误信息。

• **msadowski**：关注非技术人员过度使用 AI 导致的问题，分享了因不合适的 AI 解决方案而产生的挫败经历。他还引用了将 LLM 输出称为 "Frankfurtian BS" 的研究，认为这个描述非常贴切。

• **simianwords**：预测工具使用会导致模型更多地出现 hallucination。他注意到在使用网络搜索工具时，模型理解能力有显著差异，并建议如果不使用工具，模型的 hallucination 可能会减少。

• **saithound**：对 OpenAI 的 o3 和 o4-mini 模型在几何群论问题上的表现感到失望，指出这些模型给出了不一致且错误的答案，甚至使用问题中不存在的假设。他认为这些模型在某些应用中表现不如旧版模型。

补充讨论：
• **serjester**：提到 o3 模型在处理代码时会遗漏重要部分，需要二次检查。
• **rzz3**：询问导致 hallucination 的技术原因，指出这是当前研究的一个活跃领域。
• **the_snooze**：质疑 LLM 系统在简单易查的用例中仍不可靠的情况下，是否适合用于非玩具应用。
• **taf2**：认为在智能与谎言之间存在细微界限，hallucination 可能是一种创造性的表现。
• **evo_9**：提出模型可能需要一种类似于人类睡眠的机制来清理错误信息。
• **czk**：建议通过更严格的奖励信号来提高模型输出的准确性，奖励模型说 "我不知道" 的情况。
• **jablongo**：讨厌需要说服 AI 它正在 hallucinating 才能继续任务的工作流程。
• **daxfohl**：认为听起来更智能的答案可能会毒化用于微调的 RLHF 结果。
• **mstipetic**：分享了一次 frustrating 的经历，模型为了证明自己的正确性而篡改计算和描述，导致用户对模型失去信任。

争议焦点：
• 模型的 hallucination 问题是否能通过技术手段解决，如改进训练机制、引入验证系统等。
• LLM 在非玩具应用中的可靠性和责任性问题。
• 工具使用对模型 hallucination 的影响以及如何平衡智能与准确性。

43732506.article_content:
OpenAI’s
recently launched o3 and o4-mini AI models
are state-of-the-art in many respects. However, the new models still hallucinate, or make things up — in fact, they hallucinate
more
than several of OpenAI’s older models.
Hallucinations have proven to be one of the biggest and most difficult problems to solve in AI, impacting
even today’s best-performing systems
. Historically, each new model has improved slightly in the hallucination department, hallucinating less than its predecessor. But that doesn’t seem to be the case for o3 and o4-mini.
According to OpenAI’s internal tests, o3 and o4-mini, which are so-called reasoning models, hallucinate
more often
than the company’s previous reasoning models — o1, o1-mini, and o3-mini — as well as OpenAI’s traditional, “non-reasoning” models, such as GPT-4o.
Perhaps more concerning, the ChatGPT maker doesn’t really know why it’s happening.
In its technical report for
o3 and o4-mini
, OpenAI writes that “more research is needed” to understand why hallucinations are getting worse as it scales up reasoning models. O3 and o4-mini perform better in some areas, including tasks related to coding and math. But because they “make more claims overall,” they’re often led to make “more accurate claims as well as more inaccurate/hallucinated claims,” per the report.
OpenAI found that o3 hallucinated in response to 33% of questions on PersonQA, the company’s in-house benchmark for measuring the accuracy of a model’s knowledge about people. That’s roughly double the hallucination rate of OpenAI’s previous reasoning models, o1 and o3-mini, which scored 16% and 14.8%, respectively. O4-mini did even worse on PersonQA — hallucinating 48% of the time.
Third-party
testing
by Transluce, a nonprofit AI research lab, also found evidence that o3 has a tendency to make up actions it took in the process of arriving at answers. In one example, Transluce observed o3 claiming that it ran code on a 2021 MacBook Pro “outside of ChatGPT,” then copied the numbers into its answer. While o3 has access to some tools, it can’t do that.
“Our hypothesis is that the kind of reinforcement learning used for o-series models may amplify issues that are usually mitigated (but not fully erased) by standard post-training pipelines,” said Neil Chowdhury, a Transluce researcher and former OpenAI employee, in an email to TechCrunch.
Sarah Schwettmann, co-founder of Transluce, added that o3’s hallucination rate may make it less useful than it otherwise would be.
Kian Katanforoosh, a Stanford adjunct professor and CEO of the upskilling startup Workera, told TechCrunch that his team is already testing o3 in their coding workflows, and that they’ve found it to be a step above the competition. However, Katanforoosh says that o3 tends to hallucinate broken website links. The model will supply a link that, when clicked, doesn’t work.
Hallucinations may help models arrive at interesting ideas and be creative in their “thinking,” but they also make some models a tough sell for businesses in markets where accuracy is paramount. For example, a law firm likely wouldn’t be pleased with a model that inserts lots of factual errors into client contracts.
One promising approach to boosting the accuracy of models is giving them web search capabilities. OpenAI’s GPT-4o with web search achieves
90% accuracy
on SimpleQA, another one of OpenAI’s accuracy benchmarks. Potentially, search could improve reasoning models’ hallucination rates, as well — at least in cases where users are willing to expose prompts to a third-party search provider.
If scaling up reasoning models indeed continues to worsen hallucinations, it’ll make the hunt for a solution all the more urgent.
“Addressing hallucinations across all our models is an ongoing area of research, and we’re continually working to improve their accuracy and reliability,” said OpenAI spokesperson Niko Felix in an email to TechCrunch.
In the last year, the broader AI industry has pivoted to focus on reasoning models after
techniques to improve traditional AI models started showing diminishing returns
. Reasoning improves model performance on a variety of tasks without requiring massive amounts of computing and data during training. Yet it seems reasoning also may lead to more hallucinating — presenting a challenge.

43732506.article_summary: OpenAI的最新模型o3和o4-mini在许多方面都是最先进的，但它们比之前的模型更容易产生“幻觉”（即编造信息）。这些幻觉问题在AI领域一直难以解决，甚至影响当前最优秀的系统。尽管o3和o4-mini在编码和数学等任务上表现更好，但由于它们输出的声明更多，也导致了更多的错误信息。内部测试显示，o3在PersonQA上的幻觉率达到33%，而o4-mini则高达48%。第三方测试也发现o3会虚构其执行的操作。尽管这些模型在某些工作流中表现出色，但其高幻觉率可能限制其在需要高精度领域的应用。OpenAI正研究通过网络搜索功能来提高准确性，但幻觉问题仍是亟待解决的挑战。

主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）的 hallucination（幻觉）问题及其相关争议

不同观点：

• **msadowski**：关注非技术人员过度使用 AI 导致的问题，分享了因不合适的 AI 解决方案而产生的挫败经历。他还引用了将 LLM 输出称为 "Frankfurtian BS" 的研究，认为这个描述非常贴切。

补充讨论：

• **rzz3**：询问导致 hallucination 的技术原因，指出这是当前研究的一个活跃领域。
• **the_snooze**：质疑 LLM 系统在简单易查的用例中仍不可靠的情况下，是否适合用于非玩具应用。
• **taf2**：认为在智能与谎言之间存在细微界限，hallucination 可能是一种创造性的表现。

• **daxfohl**：认为听起来更智能的答案可能会毒化用于微调的 RLHF 结果。
• **mstipetic**：分享了一次 frustrating 的经历，模型为了证明自己的正确性而篡改计算和描述，导致用户对模型失去信任。

争议焦点：
• 模型的 hallucination 问题是否能通过技术手段解决，如改进训练机制、引入验证系统等。
• LLM 在非玩具应用中的可靠性和责任性问题。

data.article_summary: 《Hands-On Large Language Models》是一本由Jay Alammar和Maarten Grootendorst撰写的实践指南，通过近300张定制图表，帮助读者掌握大型语言模型的实用工具和概念。本书代码库包含各章节示例，建议使用Google Colab运行以获得最佳体验。内容涵盖语言模型基础、文本分类、提示工程、高级文本生成、多模态模型等主题。书中还提供了环境设置指南和代码示例，适合希望深入理解和应用语言模型的读者。多位专家推荐此书，称其兼具理论与实践，是学习大型语言模型的宝贵资源。

Hands-On Large Language Models
Welcome! In this repository you will find the code for all examples throughout the book
Hands-On Large Language Models
written by
Jay Alammar
and
Maarten Grootendorst
which we playfully dubbed:
"The Illustrated LLM Book"
Through the visually educational nature of this book and with
almost 300 custom made figures
, learn the practical tools and concepts you need to use Large Language Models today!
The book is available on:
Amazon
Shroff Publishers (India)
O'Reilly
Kindle
Barnes and Noble
Goodreads
Table of Contents
We advise to run all examples through Google Colab for the easiest setup. Google Colab allows you to use a T4 GPU with 16GB of VRAM for free. All examples were mainly built and tested using Google Colab, so it should be the most stable platform. However, any other cloud provider should work.
Chapter
Notebook
Chapter 1: Introduction to Language Models
Chapter 2: Tokens and Embeddings
Chapter 3: Looking Inside Transformer LLMs
Chapter 4: Text Classification
Chapter 5: Text Clustering and Topic Modeling
Chapter 6: Prompt Engineering
Chapter 7: Advanced Text Generation Techniques and Tools
Chapter 8: Semantic Search and Retrieval-Augmented Generation
Chapter 9: Multimodal Large Language Models
Chapter 10: Creating Text Embedding Models
Chapter 11: Fine-tuning Representation Models for Classification
Chapter 12: Fine-tuning Generation Models
Tip
You can check the
setup
folder for a quick-start guide to install all packages locally and you can check the
conda
folder for a complete guide on how to setup your environment, including conda and PyTorch installation.
Note that the depending on your OS, Python version, and dependencies your results might be slightly differ. However, they
should this be similar to the examples in the book.

data.title: JavaScript Views, the Hard Way – A Pattern for Writing UI
data.author: voat
data.article_summary: 《Writing JavaScript Views the Hard Way》介绍了一种不依赖框架（如React、Vue）直接用JavaScript编写视图的方法，强调性能、零依赖、可移植性、可维护性等优势。该方法通过使用直接的指令式代码来避免"意大利面条式代码"问题，不依赖抽象层，确保最佳性能。它没有外部依赖，适合跨框架共享组件，且易于调试，因为堆栈跟踪更浅。该模式遵循"props向下，事件向上"的模型，确保数据流动清晰。代码示例展示了如何创建一个简单的"Hello World"组件，通过模板克隆和状态更新函数来管理视图。这种方法适用于所有浏览器，甚至包括旧版本如IE9，具有很高的可维护性和性能优势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：前端开发中使用不同方法处理UI状态和渲染的优劣

不同观点：
• **efortis** 支持手动操作DOM，并展示了一个不依赖现代框架的实现示例。使用`h`函数模拟类似React的`createElement`，并通过直接替换DOM内容来更新界面。强调了这种方式的简单和直接。
• **athrowaway3z** 认为使用`state`变量是反模式，主张使用Web Components并将状态直接存储在DOM元素中。这种方式避免了额外的状态管理，通过操作DOM元素的属性来实现状态更新。
• **epolanski** 分享了使用原生TypeScript和DOM操作的经验，质疑现代前端框架的“最佳实践”，认为这种方式更简单、更具乐趣，且性能更好。
• **zffr** 对基于约定的设计模式表示怀疑，认为这种方法缺乏强制性，容易导致代码不可预测和维护困难。相比之下，类基于的UI框架如UIKit能提供更可预测和可维护的代码。
• **edflsafoiewq** 认为这种手动更新代码的方式正是响应式视图库所要取代的，暗示现代框架在处理状态更新和渲染上更为高效。
• **dsego** 提到这种方法类似于Backbone.js，并提供了MVC模式的参考资料，暗示这种模式在现代前端开发中仍有应用。
• **yumaikas** 正在开发一个类似的JS工具包，虽然尚未实现完全的响应式和双向绑定，但强调了其方法的灵活性和易用性。
• **lylejantzi3rd** 分享了使用函数和模板字面量的方式，指出这种方式在函数嵌套和组合上的困难。
• **atum47** 讲述了自己开发自定义框架的经历，并提到使用自制的轻量级框架tiny.js，展示了其在个人项目中的应用。
• **seumars** 指出UI开发的难点在于状态管理，而非框架本身，强调了状态管理方法的多样性和复杂性。
• **admiralrohan** 认为这种方式在性能上有优势，表示会关注相关项目的发展。
• **triyambakam** 喜欢使用纯HTML、CSS和JS开发，强调了这种方式的可移植性和可操作性，认为React等框架对简单项目而言过于沉重。
• **dullcrisp** 质疑为何不使用Web Components，暗示可能是因为Web Components基于类，不如函数式组件灵活。

补充讨论：
• **Web Components** 的使用和其基于类的特性引起了讨论，部分开发者如 **athrowaway3z** 和 **dullcrisp** 对其持不同看法。
• **状态管理** 是讨论的核心，不同开发者提出了不同的方法，包括使用DOM作为单一状态源、自定义框架、以及使用纯DOM操作。
• **框架 vs 原生开发** 的争论贯穿整个讨论，部分开发者如 **epolanski** 和 **triyambakam** 更倾向于原生开发，认为其更简单、性能更好。
• **代码的可维护性和可预测性** 是争议的焦点，如 **zffr** 对基于约定的设计模式的质疑。

matthewp / views-the-hard-way Public Notifications You must be signed in to change notification settings Fork 0 Star 34 JavaScript views; done as painfully as possible 34 stars 0 forks Branches Tags Activity Star Notifications You must be signed in to change notification settings matthewp/views-the-hard-way main Branches Tags Go to file Code Folders and files Name Name Last commit message Last commit date Latest commit History 16 Commits bin bin examples examples readme.md readme.md View all files Repository files navigation Writing JavaScript Views the Hard Way Learn how to build views in plain JavaScript in a way that is maintainable, performant, and fun. Writing JavaScript Views the Hard Way is inspired by such books as Learn C the Hard Way . What is this? Writing JavaScript Views the Hard Way is a pattern for writing JavaScript views. It is meant to serve as an alternative to using frameworks and libraries such as React , Vue and lit-html . It is a pattern , not a library. This document explains how to write views in such a way as to avoid the spaghetti code problems that commonly occur when writing low-level imperative code. We call this technique the hard way because it askews abstractions in favor of directness. Advantages over frameworks There are several reasons why you might be interested in writing your views the hard way: Performance : Writing JavaScript Views the Hard Way uses direct imperative code, so there are no unnecessary operations performed. Whether a hot or cold path, using this technique ensures nearly the best possible performance you can get in JavaScript. 0 dependencies : This technique uses no dependencies, so your code will never have to be upgraded. Have you ever used a library that released a breaking change that took you a day to upgrade? You'll never experience that problem again. Portability : Code written with simple imperative views is portable to any framework. That makes it perfect for low-level components that you might want to share with several framework communities. But I recommend using it on full apps as well. Maintainability : Despite the reputation of imperative code being difficult to maintain, views written with Writing JavaScript Views the Hard Way are extremely maintainable. This is because they follow strict conventions (you'll learn these later). These conventions ensure you always know where to look in a view. Additionally it follows a props down, events up model that makes data sharing straight-forward. Browser support : Code written in this manner is supported by all browsers; full-stop. We do use events to make passing data back up the component tree and our examples use a newer, nicer API, to do that, but you can use an older technique (discussed in the compatibility section) to get you back to at least IE9. But if you want to go further back than that even, substitute passing functions as props instead of using events and you can use this technique in IE6 if you want. And it will be by far the most performant solution you'll find for old browsers. Easier to debug : Using this approach stack traces become shallow (usually only a few function calls). This is because there are no layers between events and your code. Everything is your code, and as long as you name your functions, you'll get incredible stack traces that make it easy to trace where something goes wrong. Functional : This doesn't differentiate the technique vs all frameworks but it's worth pointing out at a benefit. Writing JavaScript Views the Hard Way is not functional in the immutable sense; there are definitely mutations; but it is functional in the sense that you're dealing with plain functions (no classes in sight) and without side-effects outside of the view's local state. The structure Enough with the arguments for now, let's talk about the structure. A view component written with Writing JavaScript Views the Hard Way looks like the following. data.title: Ocean Iron Fertilization
data.article_summary:
铁施肥是一种碳去除（CDR）技术，通过向海洋表面添加铁来刺激浮游植物的生长，从而吸收大气中的二氧化碳。浮游植物依赖光合作用生长，而在开阔洋区，铁是限制其生长的关键营养素。自然现象如撒哈拉沙漠的尘暴或火山喷发会带来铁，导致大规模浮游植物爆发，显著减少大气中的二氧化碳。研究显示，如2008年喀萨托奇火山喷发和2019-2020年澳大利亚山火后的藻华事件，均移除了大量碳。

科学家在1990年代和2000年代初进行了一系列铁施肥实验，发现添加铁确实促进了浮游植物爆发，尤其是硅藻的增长。硅藻死亡后更易沉入深海，从而长期封存碳。然而，铁的利用效率和碳沉降深度仍需进一步研究。尽管铁施肥有潜力缓解气候变化，但其生态影响和实际效果仍待验证。

Iron fertilization is a Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) technique that would artificially add iron to the ocean’s surface to stimulate growth of phytoplankton. Scientists are researching the viability of this technique to mitigate climate change. Illustration by Jack Cook, ©Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution
What is iron fertilization?
All organisms require nutrients to live and grow, and those living in the open ocean are no exception. Tiny phytoplankton drift on the water’s surface, converting sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide from the atmosphere into food and oxygen. Like other photosynthetic organisms, such as land plants, these tiny algae and cyanobacteria require nutrients for photosynthesis to occur. On land, nitrogen and phosphorous are often the limiting nutrients, but in many parts of the open ocean, these nutrients are generally available. It’s other, trace nutrients that are missing, and iron is one of the key players in this system.
Adding small amounts of iron to the ocean’s surface can trigger a bloom of phytoplankton big enough to be seen from space. Such additions happen naturally, such as when winds blow dust from the Sahara Desert or ash from a volcanic eruption. When the plume of dust or ash settles over the ocean’s surface, it triggers massive blooms of phytoplankton that remove substantial amounts of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. Iron fertilization is a Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) technique that would mimic this natural system, artificially adding iron to the ocean’s surface to stimulate growth of phytoplankton.
The oceans are often naturally fertilized by dust storms like this one in 2003, which covered a vast swath of the Atlantic Ocean with a plume of iron-rich dust from the Sahara Desert, extending more than 1,000 miles (1,600 kilometers), from the Cape Verde Islands (lower left) to the Canary Islands (top center).
(Image courtesy of Jacques Descloitres, MODIS Rapid Response Team, © National Aeronautic and Space Administration)
Why could iron fertilization be important for climate change?
Because iron is a micronutrient, phytoplankton need only trace amounts for it to have a massive impact. Ash from the 2008 eruption of Kasatochi in the Aleutian Islands created an algal bloom that is estimated to have removed 10 million tons of carbon from the sunlit zone. Soot from the 2019-2020 Australian wildfires caused a bloom between New Zealand and South America that may have removed as much as 150 to 300 million tons of carbon.
Ice core records also show a link between iron-rich dust and changes in climate. During times when large amounts of dust settled over the ocean, global temperatures dropped, with an estimated 60 billion tons of carbon drawn out of the atmosphere during these events. Many scientists argue that the iron dust contributed, at least in part, to the development of past glacial periods.
If relatively small amounts of iron can be added to the ocean’s surface to effectively remove large amounts of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, iron fertilization has the potential to play a pivotal role in reducing additional impacts associated with climate change. But it will only work if the carbon removed from the atmosphere sinks to the ocean depths, where it will be locked away for at least a century. This would buy time for a full transition from fossil-fuels to renewable sources of energy.
THE IRON-CLIMATE CONNECTION?Climate records extracted from ice at the Vostok station in Antarctica extend back 400,000 years. They consistently link low atmospheric carbon dioxide levels (top) with low air temperatures (middle), and high levels of iron-rich dust (bottom)?and vice versa. That supports the ?iron hypothesis.?
(Figure by J.R. Petit, et al.,
Nature
)
What are ocean scientists doing to employ iron fertilization?
In the 1990s and early 2000s, a series of experiments tested iron fertilization in the open ocean. These tests consistently found that adding iron led to phytoplankton blooms, However, the extent to which that carbon sank to the depths wasn’t always measured, and the phytoplankton were not able to use all of the iron for growth before the mineral sank.
Researchers did document changes in phytoplankton communities, with diatoms becoming more abundant than many other types of phytoplankton. These algae can be up to 1,000 times larger than cyanobacteria, allowing them to take up more carbon dioxide via photosynthesis. Diatoms create silica-based glass-like shells that add weight, increasing the likelihood that they will sink faster than other, smaller phytoplankton when they die. Their fast growth rates and loss to the deep sea bodes well for potential removal of carbon from the atmosphere and its sequestration deeper in the ocean.

data.title: High time to tackle drug-resistant fungal infections
data.author: pmags
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了耐药真菌感染的日益严重的威胁，尤其是*Candida auris*，这种酵母菌常对消毒剂和抗真菌药物具有耐药性，感染死亡率高达30%-60%。全球每年约有380万人死于真菌感染，且这一数字在过去十年中几乎翻倍。尽管真菌感染问题严重，但在抗菌素耐药性讨论中常被忽视。世界卫生组织的两份报告指出，目前仅有三种药物处于晚期临床试验阶段，用于应对最具威胁的真菌。文章还提到，开发抗真菌药物面临诸多挑战，包括真菌细胞与人类细胞的相似性，以及真菌耐药机制与细菌的不同。此外，农业中广泛使用的杀菌剂可能导致医学中使用的抗真菌药物产生耐药性，需通过政策协调解决。一些国家已采取措施限制对人类抗菌素有风险的杀菌剂使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：真菌感染与抗真菌药物的挑战

不同观点：
• **气候变化与真菌耐热性**：[nabla9]指出，全球气温上升正促使真菌适应更高的温度，从而能够在人体温度下生存和繁殖。这种适应性可能通过其他哺乳动物（如猪、牛、家禽）传播给人类，增加人畜共患病的风险。

• **药物研发进展**：[asah]提到Amplyx制药公司的fosmanogepix具有广谱抗真菌活性，目前处于III期临床试验阶段，显示出对抗真菌感染的潜力。

• **感染死亡率与时间框架**：[Retr0id]对高死亡率提出疑问，询问是否应明确感染后死亡的时间范围。

• **真菌感染的全球威胁与政策应对**：[pmags]引用《自然》杂志的数据，指出每年约有380万人死于真菌感染，且这一数字在过去十年中几乎翻倍。真菌感染对公共卫生的威胁日益严重，但并未得到足够重视。

• **抗真菌药物耐药性的不可避免性**：[Out_of_Characte]认为抗真菌药物耐药性是不可避免的，部分原因是现代农业方式为真菌和细菌的进化提供了理想环境，如大面积单一作物种植和单一抗真菌喷雾的使用。

• **加速抗真菌药物研发的可能性**：[badmonster]提出如何创造一个“mRNA时刻”来加速抗真菌药物的研发和发现，并询问是否有如AI药物发现、CRISPR筛选、生物铸造厂等平台可以改变经济效益。

• **非传统应对策略与耐药性传播**：[alganet]半开玩笑地提出让较无害的真菌变种传播，以对抗更具威胁性的真菌，并质疑过度清洁是否反而促进了耐药菌和真菌的繁衍。

• **手术中的真菌感染风险**：[jasfi]指出外科手术中存在感染致命真菌的风险，并询问治疗选择。

• **农业抗真菌剂对人类病原体的影响机制**：[TZubiri]询问农业抗真菌剂如何影响人类病原体，是选择耐药真菌还是通过摄入残留的唑类药物产生免疫。

• **人类生活方式与真菌感染的关系**：[metalman]认为人类生活方式和饮食习惯的改变，使得真菌感染问题更加严峻，并提到自身注意到食物中真菌味道增加的现象。

• **药物治疗的局限性**：[LinuxBender]预测未来几十年人们会发现药物并非对抗真菌感染的最佳方法。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：真菌感染的严重性、抗真菌药物的研发进展及其应对策略的有效性是主要争议点。不同评论者对当前药物治疗的潜力和未来方向存在不同看法。

• 重要论据：气候变化对真菌耐热性的影响、农业实践对抗真菌耐药性的推动作用、真菌感染死亡率的上升趋势，以及创新药物研发平台的潜力。

High time to tackle drug-resistant fungal infections
Download PDF
Twitter
Facebook
Email
You have full access to this article via your institution.
Download PDF
There are concerns that the widespread use of fungicides to spray agricultural crops could lead to fungal resistance to similar compounds used in medicine.
Credit: Andrii Yalanskyi/Getty
C
andida auris
is a frightening yeast. It was first identified in 2009, in the inflamed ear canal of a Tokyo-based septuagenarian
1
. Within a decade, researchers had found the yeast in ill people around the world.
C. auris
is often
resistant to disinfectants and antifungal drugs
, and can be difficult to kill. Between 30% and 60% of the people it infects will die.
Around 3.8 million people die each year of infections caused by
C. auris
and other fungi. Annual deaths caused by fungal infections have nearly doubled in the past decade.
Understanding pathogen emergence through the lens of
Candida auris
Pathogenic fungi pose unique challenges, and overcoming them will require innovative approaches to both science and policy. Yet, despite the
growing global threat
posed by drug-resistant fungi, such infections rarely loom large in discussions of antimicrobial resistance. Two World Health Organization (WHO) reports published this month (see
go.nature.com/3rniybw
) — the organization’s first analyses of tests and treatments for fungal infections — highlight the result of that neglect. Only three drugs to tackle the fungi that pose the biggest threat to human health are in late-stage clinical trials. Researchers, policymakers and industry must quickly act together to bolster the treatment pipeline and also to protect the potency of the antifungal drugs already in use.
Severe fungal infections typically strike the most vulnerable, such as people with weakened immune systems or chronic respiratory conditions. Better, cheaper tests are needed to diagnose fungal infections in a timely way, and to determine whether the fungi responsible are drug-resistant. Diagnoses are often delayed, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, where fungal infections are common. This can lead to inappropriate treatment and contribute to resistance to antimicrobial drugs.
Designing such drugs is also difficult. Fungal cells are more similar to human cells than to bacteria, suggesting that an antifungal compound could also be toxic to people. And lessons learnt from bacterial antimicrobial resistance do not always apply: when drug resistance emerges in fungi, it often does so through molecular mechanisms different from those that bacteria use to overcome antibiotics.
Candida
yeast cells imaged with a scanning electron microscope.
Credit: Steve Gschmeissner/SPL
All of this means that it is crucial to invest in basic research to better understand which cellular pathways can be targeted in fungi without harming human cells. Last month, for example, researchers reported a compound made by bacteria that targets fungal cell membranes through a new mechanism, yet is relatively non-toxic to human cells grown in culture
2
. Studies of fungal genetics, meanwhile, will be crucial to the detection of emerging pathogenic strains and drug resistance, as well as the design of new antifungal drugs.
New antifungal breaks the mould
Drug-resistant fungal infections are fairly rare, making them difficult and expensive to study. What’s more, people who contract serious fungal infections often have other health conditions that can make it hard to determine the safety of an experimental treatment. One way to facilitate clinical trials would be to establish clinical trial networks covering many institutions. These networks could standardize protocols and diagnostic tools, as well as drawing participants from a wide geographic area.
Perhaps the biggest policy challenge will be to address a major potential source of drug resistance: agriculture. Some antifungal medicines are similar to the fungicides that farmers spray to protect crops, so the widespread use of fungicides could result in fungal resistance to similar compounds used in medicine. Overcoming this problem will require stakeholders to join together and find ways of protecting both food security and human health.
Some countries are already taking steps in this direction. India has banned two antibiotics from being used for plant protection, because alternatives that pose less danger to human antimicrobials are available. The US Environmental Protection Agency has proposed including the risks of promoting resistance to antifungals in its assessment of the potential health impacts of new fungicides.
Global warming could drive the emergence of new fungal pathogens
And, earlier this year, representatives of five European Union health and environmental agencies published a report on the threat that fungicide use in agriculture poses to a class of medicines used to treat infection with
Aspergillus
fungi

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：防止手术中遗留异物的问题及解决方案

不同观点：
• rkagerer：提到不同行业（航空、日本火车、消防部门）采用的一些有效方法，如检查清单、指差呼唤以及双人检查机制，认为这些文化驱动的技术可以在医疗行业中得到应用，减少人为错误。
• 7a1c9427：引用了英国国家健康服务体系（NHS）的数据，指出在英国每年约2100万例手术中，发生遗留异物的概率为0.002%，即大约每5万例手术发生一次。通过数据表明此类事件较为罕见，但仍然存在。
• leguminous：分享了一次亲身经历，护士通过清点海绵等物品发现了问题，并建议由非手术人员进行清点，避免手术医生因专注而忽视遗留物品。
• hhh：讲述了其母亲在手术中被遗留纱布的经历，指出部分医生操作粗心大意，且该问题在某些医生中可能是反复发生的。
• keepamovin：建议使用“检查入/出清单”，由其他工作人员管理并进行双重检查，甚至提出使用RFID技术进行追踪。
• iancmceachern：确认了手术中清点物品的标准化程序，表明已有预防措施。
• selcuka：建议使用图像处理和机器学习技术，通过摄像头监控手术过程，自动检测遗留物品，提出技术解决方案。
• logicchains：指出医生工会阻止信息公开，使得患者无法根据手术医生的表现做出明智选择，缺乏市场激励机制来促使医生提高操作标准。
• Hojojo：对其他国家的情况表示好奇，希望了解遗留异物问题在欧洲、亚洲、墨西哥或加拿大的发生频率。
• bell-cot：认为美国的外科医生缺乏问责机制，且对改进操作标准兴趣不大，批评了医疗精英阶层的特权问题。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了不同国家和行业的安全措施对比，如英国的强制报告制度。
• 提出了技术解决方案，如RFID和机器学习技术，展示了技术在防止医疗错误中的潜在应用。
• 争议的焦点包括遗留异物问题的发生频率及其严重性，以及是否有足够的机制来促使医生提高操作标准和责任心。

data.article_summary: 文章介绍了利用人工智能（AI）设计新型抗蛇毒蛋白的创新方法。全球每年约200万人遭受蛇咬伤，导致超过10万人死亡及大量终身残疾，但传统抗毒血清生产成本高、速度慢、副作用多且效果有限。为解决此问题，研究人员通过AI设计出能中和蛇毒毒素的小型稳定蛋白，重点针对α-神经毒素和细胞毒素。他们使用RFdiffusion和ProteinMPNN等计算工具生成并优化蛋白结合剂，最终开发出三种主要结合蛋白——SHRT、LNG和CYTX，分别针对不同蛇毒，并在毒素中和实验中展现良好效果。这些AI设计的蛋白具有高热稳定性和溶解性，适合资源匮乏地区使用，为抗蛇毒治疗带来新希望。

主要讨论点：围绕机器学习模型、蛋白质发现、蛇毒研究及其社会影响的多元观点

不同观点：
• [对机器学习模型的关注]  
  - **rsedgwick**：除了大型语言模型（LLMs），其他机器学习模型如RFdiffusion在蛋白质发现等领域也有突破性应用。尽管LLMs因其强大的能力吸引了大量关注，但传统神经网络模型依然具有重要价值。例子：RFdiffusion模型在蛇毒中和方面的成功。

• [对死亡人数的质疑]  
  - **AIPedant**：对评论中提到的蛇咬伤导致“超过10万人死亡”提出质疑，引用论文和维基百科的数据，认为更准确的估计在40,000-80,000之间，尽管这也是一个很大的数字。

• [对制药公司专利问题的担忧]  
  - **aurizon**：担心大型制药公司会试图对AI设计的蛋白质结构申请专利，从而使印度和非洲的蛇咬伤受害者支付高昂费用。提出这些AI模型设计的蛋白质结构可能不受专利保护，且可能具有较长的室温保存期限，适合资源匮乏地区使用。

• [对AI在生物化学 warfare中的潜在威胁]  
  - **ReptileMan**：认为AI不仅能设计蛇毒中和剂，还可能被用于设计毒剂，从而在AI时代带来生物和化学战争的潜在威胁。

• [对其他毒物研究的兴趣]  
  - **speed_spread**：提出是否可以将类似方法应用于蜘蛛毒物的研究。

• [对蛇类的负面看法]  
  - **rvz**：对蛇类持负面看法，认为蛇对人类社会贡献不大，且对人类构成威胁，无法与它们进行理性互动。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了多个与AI和蛇毒研究相关的重要议题，包括技术进步的社会影响、数据准确性的质疑、以及对特定动物的看法。
• 争议的焦点包括蛇咬伤致死人数的准确性和AI在生物化学 warfare中的潜在威胁。
• 还涉及到对制药公司专利行为的担忧，以及对AI应用扩展到其他毒物研究的兴趣。
