README.md
MCP Run Python
Model Context Protocol
server to run Python code in a sandbox.
The code is executed using
Pyodide
in
Deno
and is therefore isolated from
the rest of the operating system.
See
https://ai.pydantic.dev/mcp/run-python/
for complete documentation.
The server can be run with
deno
installed using:
deno run \
-N -R=node_modules -W=node_modules --node-modules-dir=auto \
jsr:@pydantic/mcp-run-python [stdio
|
sse
|
warmup]
where:
-N -R=node_modules -W=node_modules
(alias of
--allow-net --allow-read=node_modules --allow-write=node_modules
)
allows network access and read+write access to
./node_modules
. These are required so pyodide can download and cache
the Python standard library and packages
--node-modules-dir=auto
tells deno to use a local
node_modules
directory
stdio
runs the server with the
Stdio MCP transport
—
suitable for running the process as a subprocess locally
sse
runs the server with the
SSE MCP transport
—
running the server as an HTTP server to connect locally or remotely
warmup
will run a minimal Python script to download and cache the Python standard library. This is also useful to
check the server is running correctly.
Here's an example of using
@pydantic/mcp-run-python
with PydanticAI:
from
pydantic_ai
import
Agent
from
pydantic_ai
.
mcp
import
MCPServerStdio
import
logfire
logfire
.
configure
()
logfire
.
instrument_mcp
()
logfire
.
instrument_pydantic_ai
()
server
=
MCPServerStdio
(
'deno'
,
args
=
[
'run'
,
'-N'
,
'-R=node_modules'
,
'-W=node_modules'
,
'--node-modules-dir=auto'
,
'jsr:@pydantic/mcp-run-python'
,
'stdio'
,
])
agent
=
Agent
(
'claude-3-5-haiku-latest'
,
mcp_servers
=
[
server
])
async
def
main
():
async
with
agent
.
run_mcp_servers
():
result
=
await
agent
.
run
(
'How many days between 2000-01-01 and 2025-03-18?'
)
print
(
result
.
output
)
#> There are 9,208 days between January 1, 2000, and March 18, 2025.w
if
__name__
==
'__main__'
:
import
asyncio
asyncio
.
run
(
main
())

data.title: Ssl.com: DCV bypass and issue fake certificates for any MX hostname
data.author: xPaw
data.article_summary: 本文报告了SSL.com在使用BR 3.2.2.4.14 DCV方法进行域验证时存在漏洞。攻击者可通过伪造TXT记录，绕过验证并为未授权的域名（如aliyun.com）颁发证书。具体步骤包括访问特定网站、创建TXT记录并选择任意邮箱进行验证，最终导致错误地将邮箱域名列入已验证域名列表。SSL.com已确认问题，暂停使用有问题的DCV方法，并承诺在2025年4月21日前提供调查报告。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：PKI（公钥基础设施）系统的现状及其存在的问题，尤其是证书颁发机构（CA）的安全性和信任问题。

不同观点：
• [Galanwe] 认为PKI概念已经名存实亡。用户被训练绕过证书警告，浏览器和操作系统之间对CA存储的争夺，企业SSL代理（如ZScaler/Intune）的中间人攻击（MitM），企业内部自签名CA，以及公共CA不负责任地颁发证书，都是导致PKI失效的原因。
• [btown] 强调CAA（Certificate Authority Authorization）记录的重要性，可以通过该记录指定可信的CA，减少不可信CA颁发证书的风险。他提供了相关工具和研究，指出只有少数网站使用CAA记录，并建议监控证书透明度日志以提高安全性。
• [0x0] 认为尽管问题严重，但攻击者只能为那些他们可以获得收件箱/用户账户的域名获取证书，尽管对像gmail.com这样的大型企业来说仍然是个大问题。
• [cmeacham98] 认为这是一个相当严重的疏忽，但对SSL.com认真对待此事表示肯定，等待调查报告的结果。
• [jenny91] 表示这是她见过的最严重的TLS问题。
• [AdamJacobMuller] 提到工程师们因要在复活节周末处理此事而受到影响，表示遗憾。

data.title: The Art of Assembly Language (2010)
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 《The Art of Assembly Language》是一本关于汇编语言编程的指南，现已由No Starch Press出版。本书适用于希望深入学习汇编语言编程的读者，并通过HLA（High-Level Assembly）语言进行教学。书中详细介绍了HLA程序的基本结构、数据声明、控制结构以及标准库的使用，并提供了多个示例程序。此外，本书还涵盖了数制系统、数据组织、逻辑运算、位操作以及浮点数和字符的表示方法。对于80x86处理器的寻址模式、内存组织、堆栈段和动态内存分配等内容，书中也进行了深入讲解。通过结合理论与实践，帮助读者全面掌握汇编语言编程技巧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于使用High Level Assembly (HLA)书籍的评价与讨论

不同观点：
• [pan69] 认为这本书的内容写得很好，但对使用HLA持保留态度，更希望书籍专注于标准的供应商编译器，因为HLA让他对书失去了兴趣。
• [gtirloni] 赞同pan69的观点，表示对HLA的内容感到失望，认为学习HLA像是学习一个更差的C语言，无法提升对汇编语言本身的理解。
• [singularity2001] 分享了自己对汇编语言的喜爱，尤其是用于修改程序的小patch，但指出由于代码签名的普及，这种乐趣已不再。同时表示，对于普通开发，汇编语言在优化方面并没有实际意义。
• [discardable_dan] 提出Zachtronics的游戏化编程手册是更好的选择，认为如果要学习一种“假”的汇编语言，不如通过视频游戏来享受学习过程，并批评了书籍中的不恰当笑话。
• [billmcneale] 直接否定HLA，认为它只是C语言的弱化版，建议如果要走这条路，不如学习LLVM。
• [revskill] 关心是否能有一个Docker环境来运行书中的汇编代码，注重实际操作环境。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于HLA的价值，部分评论者认为HLA无助于学习真正的汇编语言，且不如学习其他更主流的技术如LLVM。
- 一些评论者对汇编语言的实用性提出质疑，特别是在现代开发环境中的应用。
- 有趣的是，discardable_dan建议将汇编学习游戏化，提供了一种新的学习方式视角。
- revskill的需求反映了对实际操作和学习环境的关注。

data.title: Vibe Coding is not an excuse for low-quality work
data.author: saikatsg
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI编码的应用及其对软件开发的影响

不同观点：
• **AI无法取代人类开发者的创造性和理解力**：[ndepoel]认为，尽管AI在原型设计和快速解决方案方面有其位置，但它无法取代人类的理解、创造力和洞察力。他们通过早期外包开发工作的例子，说明过度依赖外部方（或AI）可能会导致更多的工作量和挫败感。
• **AI生成的代码质量问题**：[frereubu]指出，AI生成的代码看似合理，但需要大量注意力去检查，因为可能存在严重缺陷。相比之下，有经验的开发者可能直接编写代码会更高效。
• **AI辅助编码对开发者成长的影响**：[smnplk]提出，AI辅助编码是否会对开发者的成长产生负面影响？他们担心这会减少短期内对开发者的需求，并质疑长期趋势。
• **软件质量的重新定义**：[alphazard]认为，软件质量应以用户视角来衡量，而不是开发过程的整洁和清晰度。他们主张用正式规格和测试方法替代传统代码质量，以适应AI的应用。
• **AI在特定用例中的价值**：[cjonas]分享了AI在其工作中的实际应用，特别是在小应用和快速迭代项目中，AI显著提高了效率和输出质量。
• **低风险场景下的AI应用**：[afiodorov]认为，在低风险或非关键项目中，低努力开发（vibe coding）是可以接受的，AI在这种场景下具有吸引力。

补充讨论：
• **LLM与软件工程的关系**：[OJFord]通过类比3D打印机与机械工程，描述了LLM在软件工程中的角色。
• **AI作为开发辅助而非替代**：[cookie_monsta]简明指出，AI应作为实习生而非替代者，这与其他讨论者观点一致。
• **AI处理繁琐任务的潜力**：[danenania]介绍了他们开发的Plandex工具，通过AI处理重复性任务和调试工作，减少开发者的负担，并提出“vibe debugging”的概念。
• **编码成本的误导性指标**：[AlexCoventry]提到按行数计算编码成本的误导性，强调应关注功能开发和可维护性。

争议焦点：

data.title: Raspberry Pi Lidar Scanner
data.author: Venn1
data.article_summary: PiLiDAR是一个DIY的360° 3D全景扫描仪项目，基于Raspberry Pi和LDRobot的LiDAR传感器（如LD06、LD19、STL27L）。其核心功能包括自定义串行驱动、CRC数据完整性检查、硬件PWM校准、2D实时可视化和导出（numpy或CSV格式）。全景功能通过Hugin软件将鱼眼照片拼接成6K的360°全景图，而3D场景功能则通过角度和偏移从2D平面构建3D场景，支持Open3D可视化和多种格式导出。项目还涉及NEMA17步进电机、A4988驱动器和3D打印部件等硬件配置，以及GPIO中断、电源管理和I2C配置等设置步骤。目前项目仍在开发中，初步结果包括单次扫描和基础点云处理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个硬件产品的设计、成本估算、技术细节及其应用潜力的讨论

不同观点：
• **godelski**：建议在提供硬件产品时，附上材料清单及成本估算链接，即使这些数据会随时间变化，但提供一个大致范围的成本有助于用户判断是否自行尝试。他还强调了文档记录的重要性，尤其是代码和硬件组件的选择，以减少后续麻烦。他提供了一些具体组件的价格示例。

• **Animats**：指出该扫描仪的最大测量距离为12米，当需要更远的距离时，成本会显著上升。他认为该设备足以用于小型机器人或辅助传感器，但在自动驾驶汽车的长距离扫描上仍有难度。

• **politelemon**：对3D空间的交互表示赞赏，但对鼠标控制的体验感到困惑，认为操作不够直观。

• **amelius**：提出一个相关问题，寻找一种廉价的方式来测量微米级精度，距离大约300毫米。

• **mannyv**：建议可以从二手机器人吸尘器中获取所需部件，并提出如何避免LIDAR设备之间的干扰问题。

• **itissid**：认为该技术在家庭装修项目中非常有用，可以生成难以到达位置的点云图。

• **Aspos**：质疑使用GY-521和MPU6050作为IMU的选择，认为它们表现较差，并询问它们在该设置中的具体用途。

• **abraae**：感慨现代技术的发展使得个人能够创造出如此先进的技术，同时也怀念过去的某些优点。

• **heljara**：对室内扫描和点云数据的后处理表示兴趣，特别是如何将LIDAR数据与摄影数据结合，以提高精度和覆盖范围，并对是否能超越摄影测量技术表示疑问。

补充讨论：
• **badmonster**：关注该技术的可扩展性和在大规模户外数据集上的性能表现，并询问是否在诸如SemanticKITTI或nuScenes等数据集上进行过测试。

• **donatj**：表示正需要类似的项目，但仍在犹豫选择哪种LIDAR扫描仪。

• **Havoc**：关注这些传感器的安全性，尤其是对眼睛的影响。

• **wkat4242**：对LIDAR技术的进步表示惊叹，之前并不了解其发展现状。

• **dheera**：认为项目的描述不够清晰，建议在开头就明确说明该设备的具体功能和类型（如全4π立体角扫描仪或360度单通道LIDAR等）。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在硬件组件的选择和成本估算的必要性（godelski与Aspos的观点），以及该技术在不同应用场景下的实用性和可扩展性（heljara与badmonster的疑问）。

Setup
Power Button (Wakeup & Shutdown)
Wakeup is hardwired to Pin 3
enable gpio-shutdown
echo "dtoverlay=gpio-shutdown" >> /boot/firmware/config.txt
if necesessary:
sudo nano /etc/systemd/logind.conf
HandlePowerKey=poweroff
enable i2c-GPIO for GY-521 Accelerometer
GY-521 (MPU 6060): Accelerometer, Gyroscope and thermometer
i2c adress: 0x68
Since GPIO3 is hardwired to the Power Button, we need to use i2c-GPIO to map custom i2c pins (
tutorial
). Unlike serial is not getting crossed, so we connect SDA-SDA and SCL-SCL.
SDA: GPIO22
SCL: GPIO27
disable ic2_arm and enable i2c-gpio in /boot/firmware/config.txt
dtparam=i2c_arm=off
dtoverlay=i2c-gpio,bus=3,i2c_gpio_delay_us=1,i2c_gpio_sda=22,i2c_gpio_scl=27
search for devices on i2c bus 3:
sudo i2cdetect -y 3
Power LED and CPU fan
# CPU fan at lower temp
echo "dtoverlay=gpio-fan,gpiopin=4,temp=45000" >> /boot/firmware/config.txt
# Power LED Heartbeat:
echo "dtparam=pwr_led_trigger=timer" >> /boot/firmware/config.txt
Scan Button: register GPIO interrupt
make script executable:
chmod +x gpio_interrupt.py
create new service for autostart
sudo nano /etc/systemd/system/pilidar.service
content:
[Unit]
Description=PiLiDAR-Button
After=network.target
[Service]
Type=simple
User=pi
Environment=LG_WD=/tmp
ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 /home/pi/PiLiDAR/gpio_interrupt.py
Restart=no
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
reload daemon, enable and start service:
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable pilidar.service
sudo systemctl start pilidar.service
check service if necessary:
sudo systemctl status pilidar.service
set Permission for UART on Raspberry Pi
temporary solution:
sudo chmod a+rw /dev/ttyS0
old solution: make it permanent by disabling password for chmod:
sudo visudo
pi ALL=(ALL:ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/chmod a+rw /dev/ttyS0
then execute the
temporary
solution from python:
import subprocess
command = "sudo chmod a+rw /dev/ttyS0"
process = subprocess.Pop

data.title: The Web Is Broken – Botnet Part 2
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了AI公司为训练模型而 aggressively 收集数据的问题，指出一些公司通过招募应用开发者，将“网络共享”SDK注入应用程序，形成僵尸网络，利用用户设备的网络带宽进行网络爬虫等活动。这些公司将用户的网络访问卖给客户，客户可以通过大量住宅和移动IP地址进行AI爬虫等操作。文章认为这种商业模式不正当，导致DDoS攻击和服务器瘫痪，尤其对小型服务影响严重。作者呼吁苹果、微软和谷歌采取行动，并建议所有形式的网络爬虫应被视为滥用行为，服务器应阻止此类活动。文章最后表达了对“AI” hype导致网络基础恶化的担忧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：第三方SDK和恶意软件分发问题，以及如何应对和预防相关威胁

不同观点：
• ChrisMarshallNY认为，应用开发者如果在其应用中包含恶意第三方SDK以牟利，应该对向用户分发恶意软件负责，即使开发者并非有意为之。他还批评了现代开发者对依赖项的过度使用，认为这给了不法分子可乘之机。
• Pesthuf强调，包含这些恶意库的应用应被恶意软件扫描器隔离，并主张建立一个公共的受感染应用列表，不论该恶意软件是否直接损害设备。
• Liftyee认为，与广告软件和间谍软件类似，"网络共享"软件应被视为潜在的不受欢迎的应用，且这种行为对按流量计费或网速较慢的用户有显著影响。他还建议建立一个公开的应用信息库，以帮助用户识别可疑应用。
• zahlman提出，所有形式的网页抓取都应被视为滥用行为，并建议服务器屏蔽所有抓取工具，认为这些工具助长了不良行为和AI炒作。
• pton_xd质疑封闭式应用商店的审查机制是否能有效防止此类恶意软件传播。
• amiga-workbench同样对应用商店的审查效率提出质疑，认为它们未能及时发现明显的恶意软件。
• reconnecting讨论了住宅IP代理的弱点，并介绍了一个正在开发的开源欺诈预防平台，该平台可检测来自住宅代理的虚假用户。
• karmanGO询问是否有人尝试整理使用这些恶意库的软件列表，以便用户避开相关应用。
• at0mic22提到HolaVPN等服务长期利用用户主机进行流量路由，但没有自己的服务器，并指出该服务将用户作为VPN节点使用。
• kastden询问是否存在已知的C&C服务器列表，可以用于Pihole等工具进行屏蔽。
• armchairhacker反驳zahlman的观点，认为并非所有网页抓取都是滥用行为，特别是那些遵循robots.txt规则并合理退避的抓取工具，并建议提供sitemap和API以方便抓取。
• arewethereyeta分享了一个能够捕获大多数恶意行为的网站链接。
• panstromek认为这种行为应违反应用商店和Google Play的规定，因为这些平台对应用内容非常挑剔。
• proxy_err认为这个问题非常复杂，需要一个专门的研究团队来解决，并提出一种阴谋论，认为大型云服务商可能利用机器人刷流量来获利。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于网页抓取是否应一律被视为滥用行为，以及应用商店在防止恶意软件传播方面的有效性。
• 讨论中多次提到建立公共信息库和屏蔽机制的必要性，以帮助用户识别和避开恶意应用。

43738603.article_content:
I guess you have all heard about the growing problem of AI companies trying to aggressively collect whatever data they can get their hands on to train their models. This has caused an explosive surge in web crawlers relentlessly hitting servers big and small. But who runs these crawlers? Turns out â it could be you!
1.
Those stealthy botnets
- How I found out about a not so new class of botnets
2.
The Web is Broken
-
Certain companies recruit app developers to create botnets by injecting ânetwork sharingâ SDKs into their apps. These botnets then use the network bandwidth of unsuspecting users of said apps to crawl the web, brute-force mail servers and other nasty things.
So there is a (IMHO) shady market out there that gives app developers on iOS, Android, MacOS and Windows money for including a library into their apps that sells users network bandwidth. Infatica
1
is just one example, there are many more.
I am 99% sure that these companies cause what effectively are DDoS attacks by aggressive AI crawlers that many webmasters have to deal with since months. This business model should simply not exist. Apple, Microsoft and Google should act.
From the
Infatica SDK page
, explaining how app developers can make money by including the Infatica SDK
What these companies then sell to
their
customers is network access through the devices/PCs that have an app with this SDK installed
2
. They are proud to tell you how you can funnel your (AI) web scraping etc through millions of rotating, residential and mobile IP addresses. Exactly the pattern we see hitting our servers.
Infatica claiming they have millions and millions of IP addresses to hand to you
What I would call âinfected usersâ are called âresidential IPsâ in this specific market
There are many
Now, again, this company is just one of many selling similar services. And they all promise that they carefully check what commands their customers send to the (IMHO) infected apps on your phone and PC. Yeah, I am sure they âdo no evilâ. And when they do, they can claim itâs not their problem because they are merely the proxy. Again, IMHO, a shady business model.
Trend Micro did some research on these companies back in 2023 and it confirms my suspicions. And I guess with AI scraping this kind of business is booming.
âThere are malicious actors who repacked freeware and shareware written by other people to conduct drive-by downloads of the Infatica peer-to-business (P2B) serviceâ
3
But IMHO (In My Humble Opinion) this also explains the explosion of bot traffic that really cripples a lot of smaller services (like my forgejo instance, that I had to make non-public).
So if you as an app developer include such a 3rd party SDK in your app to make some money â you are part of the problem and I think you should be held responsible for delivering malware to your users, making them botnet members.
Unfortunately it is next to impossible for normal users to detect the inclusion of such shady SDKs and the network traffic they cause. Not even mentioning how hard this is for admins of (small) web servers.
I already blogged about this
back in February 2025
but I think it is better to put what I have learned since then in this new post. I guess it wonât be my last on this topic.
See for yourself!
If you want to feel really dirty, go to
https://proxyway.com/reviews?e-filter-da2a7bc-reviews_categories=proxy-providers
for a collection of reviews on these services. Itâs a huge market and I am 100% convinced that âAIâ web scraping is currently the biggest âgrowthâ driver for these companies.
And when I see that quite some of them rely on injecting SDKs into 3rd party apps to âextendâ their âReachâ and fill their pools of âresidential proxiesâ, I would call out these companies for distributing malware and creating botnets. But thatâs just my personal opinion. I am sure they are all legit.
Page 1 of 3 with reviews of âresidential proxyâ providers
My conclusion
I am now of the opinion that
every
form of web-scraping should be considered abusive behaviour and web servers should block all of them. If you think your web-scraping is acceptable behaviour, you can thank these shady companies and the âAIâ hype for moving you to the bad corner.
Thank you for your time and interest! I hope it helps you understand why web crawlers have become a real problem and how this is more and more an attack on the foundation of the Web as it was intended to be. This âresidential proxyâ business is just one part of this. And we webmasters/admins can only try to block. It is getting more and more difficult to keep up with these waves. Thanks âAIâ, I guess?

43738603.article_summary: 文章讨论了AI公司为训练模型而 aggressively 收集数据的问题，指出一些公司通过招募应用开发者，将“网络共享”SDK注入应用程序，形成僵尸网络，利用用户设备的网络带宽进行网络爬虫等活动。这些公司将用户的网络访问卖给客户，客户可以通过大量住宅和移动IP地址进行AI爬虫等操作。文章认为这种商业模式不正当，导致DDoS攻击和服务器瘫痪，尤其对小型服务影响严重。作者呼吁苹果、微软和谷歌采取行动，并建议所有形式的网络爬虫应被视为滥用行为，服务器应阻止此类活动。文章最后表达了对“AI” hype导致网络基础恶化的担忧。
43738603.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：第三方SDK和恶意软件分发问题，以及如何应对和预防相关威胁

不同观点：
• ChrisMarshallNY认为，应用开发者如果在其应用中包含恶意第三方SDK以牟利，应该对向用户分发恶意软件负责，即使开发者并非有意为之。他还批评了现代开发者对依赖项的过度使用，认为这给了不法分子可乘之机。
• Pesthuf强调，包含这些恶意库的应用应被恶意软件扫描器隔离，并主张建立一个公共的受感染应用列表，不论该恶意软件是否直接损害设备。
• Liftyee认为，与广告软件和间谍软件类似，"网络共享"软件应被视为潜在的不受欢迎的应用，且这种行为对按流量计费或网速较慢的用户有显著影响。他还建议建立一个公开的应用信息库，以帮助用户识别可疑应用。

• amiga-workbench同样对应用商店的审查效率提出质疑，认为它们未能及时发现明显的恶意软件。
• reconnecting讨论了住宅IP代理的弱点，并介绍了一个正在开发的开源欺诈预防平台，该平台可检测来自住宅代理的虚假用户。
• karmanGO询问是否有人尝试整理使用这些恶意库的软件列表，以便用户避开相关应用。

• kastden询问是否存在已知的C&C服务器列表，可以用于Pihole等工具进行屏蔽。
• armchairhacker反驳zahlman的观点，认为并非所有网页抓取都是滥用行为，特别是那些遵循robots.txt规则并合理退避的抓取工具，并建议提供sitemap和API以方便抓取。

data.title: Unpowered SSD endurance investigation finds data loss and performance issues
data.author: progval
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了SSD在断电情况下长时间存放数据时可能出现的数据丢失问题，尤其是用于备份或存储重要文件时。TechTuber HTWingNut进行了一项实验，测试了四块SATA SSD在断电两年后的数据完整性。实验包括两块“全新”和两块“磨损”的SSD，其中磨损的驱动器写入数据量远超其耐久度额定值。第一年的测试没有发现问题，但第二年测试显示“磨损”的SSD出现了文件损坏和性能下降，而“全新”的SSD尽管数据完整，但错误校正值较高，暗示潜在问题。文章提醒用户定期刷新备份以防数据丢失。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：SSD的耐用性及其作为长期存储的适用性

不同观点：
• **jauntywundrkind**：提到一个128GB的SSD写了280TB数据，远超其额定寿命，但认为即使是廉价驱动器，其额定耐用性也不算太低。同时讨论了温度敏感性问题，计划将系统放在炎热的阁楼中，不确定高温对驱动器的影响。
• **rkagerer**：表示不会购买无品牌SSD，曾遇到过数据损坏问题，并通过实验验证了多个SSD的不可靠性。
• **stego-tech**：认为SSD作为冷存储风险大，驱动器使用越多且长期不通电会降低其可靠性。呼吁推出价格适中的LTO驱动器，供消费者和 enthusiasts 使用。
• **bityard**：认为SSD不适合长期存储是显而易见的事实，无需争议。
• **ein0p**：确认SSD不适合冷存储，数据需要定期通电保持，且提到硬件加密密钥的闪存也需要注意。
• **0manrho**：指出使用劣质无品牌SSD得出的结论不具代表性，强调不同类型闪存驱动器之间的巨大差异，并提到通过规模化使用廉价驱动器可以提高可靠性和性能，但这需要相当的研究和投资。
• **jeffbee**：指出编程温度对SSD耐用性的影响，视频中多个SSD同时安装导致温度变化，影响了实验结果。
• **csdvrx**：建议长期存储使用硬盘，尤其是CMR硬盘，并提到高性能需求可选择SLC驱动器或通过修改固件实现。同时提醒不要信任过于新的驱动器，因为可能未经过充分测试。

补充讨论：
• SSD的温度敏感性和通电状态对数据保持的影响是一个重要讨论点，不同用户对如何处理这些问题有不同见解。
• 对无品牌和廉价SSD的不信任普遍存在，许多用户通过实验和实际经验验证了其不可靠性。
• 有用户呼吁价格适中的长期存储解决方案，如LTO驱动器，认为现有消费级SSD不适合。
• 讨论中提到了不同类型闪存驱动器的巨大差异，建议在选择时需注意区分。
• 对新技术的怀疑态度，尤其是基于未充分测试的新驱动器的使用。

43739028.article_content:
(Image credit: HTWingNut)
You may not know it, but SSDs will lose data after a period of time if they are simply left unplugged, which can be a serious threat to your data if you store backups or precious files on unplugged SSDs. A year-two update on the
how long can SSDs store data unpowered
video series is another reminder about the importance of regularly refreshing your backups with a bit of juice. The tests consist of storing data on an SSD and then leaving it unplugged for years to see the impact on the stored data.
As a reminder, an SSD's endurance rating is calculated based on how long it can store data if left unplugged after a certain amount of data has been written, hence the importance of this testing.
TechTuber HTWingNut is back with a report on his modest experiment involving a quartet of SATA SSDs. The key finding was that the two-year-old, well-worn drive exhibited noticeable performance degradation and was affected by a handful of corrupt files. These are signs that this particular SSD was on its way to silicon heaven. HTWingNut's video is an update on an episode from a year earlier, and further updates are promised.
You may like
World Backup Day: A reminder to protect against data loss
Seagate hard drive controversy persists as scammers discover methods to alter reliability metrics
How Long Can SSD Store Data Unpowered? Year 2 Update - YouTube
Watch On
The four tested 'Leven JS-600' branded SSDs are basically bog-standard no-name units. HTWingNut says they are all TLC SSDs of 128GB capacity and rated to withstand 60 TB of written data. Every drive has 100GB of files containing random data, with hash values for all the content provided for later verification.
The two 'Fresh' samples have barely been used; perhaps only the 100GB data set was put on there and verified, and that's it. Meanwhile, the 'Worn' drives have been subjected to 280 terabytes of written data churn, much more than their rated 60 Terabytes Written (TBW) endurance rating..
If you watch the previous
year-one video
, you will have seen there were no issues with either 'Worn' or 'Fresh' drives. However, time has now taken its toll. Let's take a look at the year-two samples in turn.
'Fresh' SSD tests
The data on this SSD, which hadn't been used or powered up for two years, was 100% good on initial inspection. All the data hashes verified, but it was noted that the verification time took a smidgen longer than two years previously. HD Sentinel tests also showed good, consistent performance for a SATA SSD.
Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware Newsletter
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Contact me with news and offers from other Future brands
Receive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors
Digging deeper, all isn't well, though. Firing up Crystal Disk Info, HTWingNut noted that this SSD had a Hardware ECC Recovered value of over 400. In other words, the disk's error correction had to step in to fix hundreds of data-based parity bits.
Seeing these errors means "the SSD is on its way out," according to HTWingNut. Indeed, if there is anything iffy about your data storage integrity, it is at least a warning. However, the errors could also have something to do with the drive being left unpowered for two years.
(Image credit: HTWingNut)
'Worn' SSD tests
As the worn SSD's data was being verified, there were already signs of performance degradation. The hashing audit eventually revealed that four files were corrupt (hash not matching). Looking at the elapsed time, it was observed that this operation astonishingly took over 4x longer, up from 10 minutes and 3 seconds to 42 minutes and 43 seconds.
Further investigations in HD Sentinel showed that three out of 10,000 sectors were bad and performance was 'spiky.' Returning to Crystal Disk Info, things look even worse. HTWingNut notes that the uncorrectable sectors count went from 0 to 12 on this drive, and the hardware ECC recovered value went from 11,745 before to 201,273 after tests on the day.
Some takeaways
In summary, the year-one fresh and well-worn drives had no issues. However, the year-two heavily worn SSD had file corruption and performance was poor. The so-called fresh drive was still good, but ECC figures still raised concern. Come back in late 2025 for the next update from HTWingNut.
We also want to say this is a very small test sample, highlighted out of our interest in the topic rather than for its hard empirical data. I have also experienced SSD data loss after leaving a Mini PC unpowered for just six months or so at my pied-à-terre in Taiwan. On return, Windows refused to boot or be repaired, but a reformat and reinstall seemed to return everything to normal.

data.title: The Icelandic Voting System (2024)
data.author: alexharri
data.article_summary: 本文简要介绍了冰岛的投票制度。冰岛采用双比例分配制度，全国划分为多个选区，每个选区有固定数量的选区席位和调整席位。选区席位通过d'Hondt法分配，根据各党派得票数和已获席位数计算商数（q），逐次分配席位。调整席位则在全国范围内根据各党派的总得票数进行二次分配，以弥补初步分配中的不均衡，优先在党派得票最多的选区增加席位。尽管该方法在理论上存在不公平性，如偏向大党，且不符合单调性标准，但冰岛及多个国家仍在使用近似方法进行席位分配。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：斯堪的纳维亚和冰岛选举制度的优缺点及其对政治文化的影响

不同观点：
• [bjornsing] 认为斯堪的纳维亚的选举制度过于注重政党，最终决定谁进入议会及如何投票的是政党高层，导致集体主义政治文化。这种制度显得不够透明，选民的个人影响力被削弱。
• [markvdb] 指出该制度的复杂性使得即使受过大学教育的人也难以完全理解，可能因此削弱对制度的信任。引用的研究支持了这一观点。
• [yorwba] 对通过比例代表制同时实现地理分布和政党投票的平衡表示兴趣，并提出是否可以引入更多维度的代表性，如种族、宗教、年龄、性别、收入和教育水平。同时也指出，过度细分可能导致选举不秘密或议会规模过大。
• [avar] 强调冰岛选举制度的“特点”是淡化选民与地方代表之间的联系，选票可能投给同一政党在其他地区的候选人，导致偏向全国性的政党政策而非地方代表性。这种制度可能导致投票权不平等。
• [themadryaner] 提供了对冰岛选举制度细节的分析，指出调整席位的分配过程复杂且存在不公平现象，如调整席位固定且不根据每次人口普查重新分配，导致选民在不同选区间的投票权重不均。

补充讨论：
• [JumpCrisscross] 提到美国州可以采用类似的全州范围分配代表模式，而不必划分国会选区。
• [krapp] 以幽默方式表达了对讨论复杂选举制度的看法。
• [dheera] 认为冰岛选举制度要求选民具备一定教育水平才能做出明智投票决定是合理的。

The Icelandic voting system
SmÃ¡ri McCarthy

English

Contents
It’s election season here in Iceland! The election is on Saturday, 30th of November, so next Saturday from when this is written.
Every time elections are upcoming, somebody inevitably asks me how the voting system here works, probably expecting a simple answer. So, here’s a stab at it.
Iceland uses a biproportional apportionment system, as do Norway, some cantons of Switzerland, some German regions, and a few other places. Such systems have a few general features:
There is some number of constituencies, each of which has:
Some number of constituency seats (CS)
Some number of adjustment seats (AS)
Technically, you could have 0 constituency seats, but most places have some. In Iceland every constituency must have either 1 or 2 adjustment seats. So like, we have Southwest with 14 seats total, of which 2 are AS, while Northwest has 7 total, 6 CS and 1 AS. These are decided after each election (for the next election) by the national electoral commission, and take into account population in each constituency, so as to try to minimize the disparity of voting power.
Divisor rules
For this kind of system, you have a divisor rule, such as d’Hondt or Sainte-Lague. We use d’Hondt in Iceland. Scandinavia uses a modified Sainte-Lague. The rule is basically a quotient between votes and seats. d’Hondt is
$q = V/(s+1)$
Where q is the quotient, V the number of votes a party gets, and s the number of seats they’ve already been allocated.
By comparison, the Sainte-Lague method is:
$q = V / (2s+1)$
Norway and Sweden use a modified Sainte-Lague, which starts at 1.5 instead of 1, so you get a sequence of 1.5, 3, 5, …. There are a number of
other divisor rules
, each optimized for a slightly different use case.
The key difference here is that by scaling up the divisor, you’re valuing each seat much higher, resulting in it becoming proportionally easier to get the first seat, etc.
It should be said that in some ways d’Hondt is the least fair of them, clearly favoring big parties, but it’s also the only such rule that actually adds up in such a way that there’s no strategic benefit to breaking a large party up into many smaller parties. You win some, you lose some.
Allocating the constituency seats
Now that we have our divisor rule, we should start allocating, by calculating each constituency’s seats.
For each constituency, each party running in that constituency starts with 0 seats, so every party’s divisor is 1 (in d’Hondt). You then look at which party has the highest quotient ($q$), and you give them a seat.
Now recalculate the quotients (really only the one you just allocated to, the others remain unchanged). Oh, look, now the party that got a seat has a lower $q$, because their divisor is bigger. So somebody else (probably) has the highest $q$. Give them a seat. Continue until all constituency seats are allocated.
Allocating the adjustment seats
This is where the fun begins – the real biproportional part. Once all the constituency seats have been allocated, the next step is to calculate for the entire country. So we add up each party’s votes over the entire country and each party’s seats over the entire country.
If there’s a cutoff (such as the 5% rule we have in Iceland), you eliminate any parties that fall under the 5% threshold from the following process (but they keep any CS they’ve already been allocated).
Now, we’ve got some total number of AS, which are to be allocated, but we are not just allocating them to the parties, we’re allocating them to parties
in constituencies
. So the task is to figure out which party deserves the next seat
and
where it is most logical for them to get a seat, given the votes they got in each constituency.
What this effectively comes down to is, once all the CS have been allocated, you figure out which parties are most deserving of seats nationally, and give them extras, ideally in the constituencies where they got the most votes. But the devil is in the details here.
It has been proven that there is one and only one mathematically sound way to calculate the results, as shown in
this paper by Balinski & DeMange
, which describes a bilinear optimization exercise aiming at minimizing entropy. Weirdly, as far as I know, only the canton of Geneva uses this correct method.
By “correct” here, we mean that the result is Exact, Relevant, Uniform, Monotonic and Homogenous, as per these axioms:
Each of these comes with a lengthy description – I’ll just refer to the paper, but basically, you don’t really want to fail any of these tests.
So it’s a bit weird that everywhere other than Geneva that uses this kind of method, including Iceland, uses an approximation method that is provably incorrect, but in different ways.
I wrote some code for the Icelandic law method
, but more about that below.

43738675.article_summary: 本文简要介绍了冰岛的投票制度。冰岛采用双比例分配制度，全国划分为多个选区，每个选区有固定数量的选区席位和调整席位。选区席位通过d'Hondt法分配，根据各党派得票数和已获席位数计算商数（q），逐次分配席位。调整席位则在全国范围内根据各党派的总得票数进行二次分配，以弥补初步分配中的不均衡，优先在党派得票最多的选区增加席位。尽管该方法在理论上存在不公平性，如偏向大党，且不符合单调性标准，但冰岛及多个国家仍在使用近似方法进行席位分配。

data.title: The Animals That Exist Between Life and Death
data.author: dnetesn
data.article_summary: 在17世纪末，自学成才的科学家安东尼·范·列文虎克通过自制的显微镜观察到了一个微观世界，他称其中的微小生物为“微动物”。1687年，他发现了一种特别的生物——轮虫，它们具有轮状附肢，生活在全球各种水环境中。他观察到，当环境干涸时，轮虫会收缩成一个皱缩的椭圆形态，称为“tun”或“xerosome”。令人惊奇的是，加水后，这些轮虫能够复活。这一发现引发了关于生命与死亡状态的哲学争论：这些生物究竟是死了还是处于一种休眠状态？范·列文虎克的观察在当时未被重视，但后来证实一些轮虫可以在干燥状态下存活多年并重新活化，挑战了生命二元论的传统观念。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：生命与死亡的定义和边界问题，特别是在连续变化的生物现象中如何界定生与死。

不同观点：
• [pdonis] 认为生命和死亡是连续变化中的近似类别，尝试在二者之间划清界限会导致例外情况。过度纠结于此是思维混乱的表现，应该接受这些类别在大多数情况下是有用的，但在边缘情况下可能会失效。

• [kvark] 提出三体问题中的脱水/复水概念可能受到了那些微小生物（如轮虫）的启发，作为在灾难中生存的技能。

• [Ghos3t] 提到《虚无主义者的世界》这本书，其中二元与非二元思维方式是一个核心主题，暗示对生命与死亡的讨论可能与更广泛的哲学主题相关。

• [ggm] 讨论了可复活状态与死亡定义的关系，提出如果一个生物能够被复活，那么其死亡的定义可能过早。并以病毒、朊病毒、线粒体为例，质疑这些生物是否应被定义为“非生命”。

• [verisimi] 认为种子与那些微小生物的状态类似，可以在休眠状态下存活多年，并提出这些生物是否可以通过反复进入初始“种子状态”来实现生命的反复激活。

• [suzzer99] 以木蛙为例，指出其心脏在冻结时停止跳动，直到解冻后再次跳动，质疑这种现象是否与讨论的生物状态类似。

• [lo_zamoyski] 认为生命与死亡可能不是唯一的生存状态，并提出死亡是存在的缺席。同时，批评了将科学发现与宗教教义对立的历史观点，认为这是过时的陈词滥调，特别是在涉及哲学和神学问题时。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于如何定义生命与死亡，特别是在面对可以进入休眠或脱水状态的生物时，传统的二元分类是否适用。
• 讨论中涉及的例子包括轮虫、病毒、种子和木蛙，这些例子都展示了生命与死亡之间的模糊边界。
• 哲学和历史的视角也被引入讨论，特别是对科学发现与宗教教义关系的批评，以及现代哲学在处理潜在性问题上的困难。

以上观点展示了在生命与死亡定义问题上的多角度思考和复杂性。

Explore
I
n the late 1600s, self-made scientist Antonie van Leeuwenhoek embarked on a project that would make him question the very nature of life and its limit. And would send ripples of philosophical and scientific quandaries through the generations that persist today. Peering through the hand-ground lenses he crafted, magnifying his subjects 275 times, the Dutch cloth merchant and naturalist was the first human to glimpse an otherworldly microcosmos where astonishing creatures seemed to defy the laws of nature and survival. He called them, adoringly, “animalcules.”

In 1687, he discovered some animalcules so peculiar in form and function that he would spend decades observing them. We now know these tiny animals, which had wheel-like appendages that van Leeuwenhoek correctly surmised were for feeding, as
rotifers
. They live in watery environments throughout the globe, from the tropics to Antarctica, in oceans, temporary puddles, and even in moisture within moss. But van Leeuwenhoek wasn’t satisfied just watching them. He decided to test these ubiquitous animals’ limits. He wanted to see what would happen to them when their surrounding aqueous environment dried up.
Other animalcules, he noted, would readily break apart or collapse in on themselves upon desiccation. But when he dried out rotifers, they each instead contracted into a shrunken, wrinkled oval, now called a “tun” or “
xerosome
.”
Philosophers are still grappling with the idea that life and death may not be the only states of being.

.
What van Leeuwenhoek discovered next went beyond anything he could have imagined: After adding water to a glass tube that contained dried sediment and rotifer tuns he’d collected from a rain gutter, van Leeuwenhoek watched in wonder through his homemade microscope as rotifers came back to life. “I examined it, and perceived some of the Animalcules lying closely heaped together,” he wrote in a
letter to the British Royal Society
. “In a short time afterwards they began to extend their bodies, and in half an hour at least a hundred of them were swimming about the glass …” As a good experimentalist, he repeated the process by drying out other rotifers and witnessing the same phenomenon numerous times—even after samples were desiccated for a month.
“These little animals, which had appeared to be completely dried and lifeless, were restored to motion upon the addition of water, as if they had never suffered any harm,” van Leeuwenhoek wrote. Microbiologists would later find that some species of rotifers are able to reanimate after up to nine years of desiccation.
According to University of California, Davis philosophy professor Cody Gilmore, van Leeuwenhoek’s observations presented a philosophical paradox beyond the biological questions they raised concerning desiccation and survival. Consider those newly identified rotifers in van Leeuwenhoek’s dried gutter sediment that apparently came back to life. The tuns, as far as the progenitor of microbiology could tell, showed no signs of living—no movement or activity or perceptible change for days, potentially weeks. Were the animals technically dead? Were they, in tun form, actually still alive but dormant, like a mammal in hibernation? Or were they in some kind of liminal, in-between state? An underlying assumption held by most people, including biologists and philosophers today, is that organisms are either alive or dead. Gilmore notes that the paradox lies in maintaining the possibility of such a binary proposition in the face of rotifers and other extremophiles that seem to occupy such a third state as they await reanimation.
TUN OF FUN:
Rotifers and other extremophiles can survive years of desiccation by entering into a state of diapause, transforming into a “tun” or “xerosome” such as this one, which likely formed from the rotifer
Macrotrachela quadricornifera.

Van Leeuwenhoek wrote that his rotifers “came back to life,” but he never hinted at whether he thought they were resurrected or if they had remained alive, apparently failing to fully realize—or being unwilling to confront—the philosophical quandary raised by his discovery. Despite acceptance from the Royal Society, his observations also failed to gain notice by his contemporaries and were shelved for years. Without a powerful enough “van Leeuwenhoek microscope” or accurate scales to precisely measure desiccation, naturalists of the day could neither replicate his observations nor dive into their implications. In fact, many of van Leeuwenhoek’s early observations were often met with skepticism. Forget about tiny, resurrecting bugs. A microcosmos of bizarre lifeforms, unseeable with the naked eye, sounded to most of his contemporaries more like fiction than reality.

data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 摄影师Joshua Rozells在澳大利亚Pinnacles Desert拍摄星空时，意外发现大量卫星轨迹污染了照片。他将343张照片合成一张图片，展示了日益严重的卫星污染问题。自2019年SpaceX启动Starlink项目以来，已有超过10,000颗卫星升空，且计划发射更多。天文学家警告，卫星数量激增加剧光污染，影响天文研究。尽管这些卫星提供重要数据，但缺乏监管可能导致问题恶化。一些组织，如国际天文学联合会的保护暗静天空中心，正呼吁规范和保护夜空。

Photo © Joshua Rozells, shared with permission
A Stunning Image of the Australian Desert Illuminates the Growing Problem of Satellite Pollution
April 18, 2025
Nature
Photography
Grace Ebert
Share
Pin
Email
Bookmark
In January 2021,
Joshua Rozells
ventured out into the Pinnacles Desert in Western Australia, intending to photograph a star trail. But after shooting for more than three hours and reviewing his images, he realized that the light patterns he captured weren’t what he had hoped for.
“There were satellite trails visible in almost every single photo,” he wrote on
Instagram
. “Instead of trying to get rid of them for a star trail, I decided to put the satellite trails together into a single image to show how polluted the night sky is becoming.”
Stitching together 343 distinct photos, Rozells illuminates a growing problem. When Elon Musk’s SpaceX launched Starlink in 2019, 60 satellites filled the skies, with a race from other companies to follow. That number
has now topped 10,000
, with tens of thousands more in the works. SpaceX alone plans to launch 40,000 more.
Rozells’ composite visually echoes pleas from astronomers, who warn that although satellites collect essential data, the staggering amount filling our skies will only worsen light pollution and our ability to study what lies beyond. Because this industry has little regulation, the problem could go unchecked.
“Thankfully, astronomers across the globe have taken notice of this growing issue and are starting to speak up,” Rozells adds. “Organisations such as the International Astronomical Union’s Center for the Protection of the Dark and Quiet Sky are advocating for the regulation and protection of the night sky.” (via
Kottke
)

43737469.article_summary: 摄影师Joshua Rozells在澳大利亚Pinnacles Desert拍摄星空时，意外发现大量卫星轨迹污染了照片。他将343张照片合成一张图片，展示了日益严重的卫星污染问题。自2019年SpaceX启动Starlink项目以来，已有超过10,000颗卫星升空，且计划发射更多。天文学家警告，卫星数量激增加剧光污染，影响天文研究。尽管这些卫星提供重要数据，但缺乏监管可能导致问题恶化。一些组织，如国际天文学联合会的保护暗静天空中心，正呼吁规范和保护夜空。

data.title: Inside ArXiv
data.author: fprog
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了由物理学教授Paul Ginsparg创建的学术预印本平台arXiv的故事。arXiv成立近35年，尽管界面简陋，但它对科学界产生了深远影响，成为数学和物理学等领域研究者的重要资源。平台允许科学家快速分享未经过同行评审的论文（预印本），加速了科研成果的传播，尤其在新冠疫情期间发挥了关键作用。虽然arXiv不进行同行评审，但有专家志愿者和自动化检查确保基本学术标准。目前，arXiv拥有超过260万篇论文，月活跃用户达500万，是许多重大科学发现的首发平台。然而，arXiv的持续运作也曾面临官僚问题、代码过时甚至间谍风波等挑战。Ginsparg将自己创建的arXiv比作“离家上大学却常回来捣乱的孩子”，反映出平台维护的复杂性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于arXiv平台的运行、发展及其面临的挑战

不同观点：
• **westurner**：认为arXiv是一个具有变革意义的学术平台，支持多种格式（如PostScript, LaTeX, PDF）的学术文章上传，强调了互联网和网络对科学的重大影响。
• **sundarurfriend**：指出arXiv作为一个公共资源，在维持运营和保持完整性方面面临挑战。当平台变大后，容易吸引试图破坏其本质的人，导致平台完整性风险增加。
• **behnamoh**：分享了个人经历，指出arXiv审核团队可能存在偏见，因其缺乏CS学位背景，论文被长时间搁置，暗示平台在评审过程中的潜在问题。
• **elashri**：调侃了一些老派物理学家的态度，暗示他们对文档和规范的忽视，反映出不同代际在学术态度上的差异。
• **Y_Y**：对arXiv近期的公关活动持怀疑态度，预言其可能会经历“enshittification”（质量下降），并提到其比GitHub寿命长。

补充讨论：
• arXiv作为一个公共学术平台，在从小型服务发展到大型平台的过程中，面临如何保持其完整性和抵御外部干扰的问题。
• 不同背景的用户对arXiv的体验和看法各异，反映了平台在审核、用户多样性和公关策略上的多重挑战。
• 对平台未来发展的担忧，尤其是如何在扩展影响力和保持质量之间取得平衡，是讨论中的一个重要关注点。

“Just when I
thought I was out, they pull me back in!” With a sly grin that I’d soon come to recognize, Paul Ginsparg quoted Michael Corleone from
The Godfather
. Ginsparg, a physics professor at Cornell University and a certified MacArthur genius, may have little in common with Al Pacino’s mafia don, but both are united by the feeling that they were denied a graceful exit from what they’ve built.
Nearly 35 years ago, Ginsparg created
arXiv
, a digital repository where researchers could share their latest findings—before those findings had been systematically reviewed or verified. Visit arXiv.org today (it’s pronounced like “archive”) and you’ll still see its old-school Web 1.0 design, featuring a red banner and the seal of Cornell University, the platform’s institutional home. But arXiv’s unassuming facade belies the tectonic reconfiguration it set off in the
scientific community
. If arXiv were to stop functioning, scientists from every corner of the planet would suffer an immediate and profound disruption. “Everybody in math and physics uses it,” Scott Aaronson, a computer scientist at the University of Texas at Austin, told me. “I scan it every night.”
Every industry has certain problems universally acknowledged as broken: insurance in health care, licensing in music, standardized testing in education, tipping in the restaurant business. In academia, it’s publishing. Academic publishing is dominated by for-profit giants like Elsevier and Springer. Calling their practice a form of thuggery isn’t so much an insult as an economic observation. Imagine if a book publisher demanded that authors write books for free and, instead of employing in-house editors, relied on other authors to edit those books, also for free. And not only that: The final product was then sold at prohibitively expensive prices to ordinary readers, and institutions were forced to pay exorbitant fees for access.
The “free editing” academic publishers facilitate is called peer review, the process by which fellow researchers vet new findings. This can take months, even a year. But with arXiv, scientists could post their papers—known, at this unvetted stage, as preprints—for instant and free access to everyone. One of arXiv’s great achievements was “showing that you could divorce the actual transmission of your results from the process of refereeing,” said Paul Fendley, an early arXiv moderator and now a physicist at All Souls College, Oxford. During crises like the Covid pandemic, time-sensitive breakthroughs were disseminated quickly—particularly by bioRxiv and medRxiv, platforms inspired by arXiv—potentially saving,
by one study’s estimate
, millions of lives.
While arXiv submissions aren’t peer-reviewed, they are moderated by experts in each field, who volunteer their time to ensure that submissions meet basic academic standards and follow arXiv’s guidelines: original research only, no falsified data, sufficiently neutral language. Submissions also undergo automated checks for baseline quality control. Without these, pseudoscientific papers and amateur work would flood the platform.
How to Get Computers—Before Computers Get You
Post-quantum algorithms, thermodynamic hardware, open source architectures, apocalypse-proof programming, and more: WIRED journeys to the freaky
frontiers of modern computing
.
In 2021, the journal Nature
declared arXiv
one of the “10 computer codes that transformed science,” praising its role in fostering scientific collaboration. (The article is behind a paywall—unlock it for $199 a year.) By a recent count, arXiv hosts more than 2.6 million papers, receives 20,000 new submissions each month, and has 5 million monthly active users. Many of the most significant discoveries of the 21st century have first appeared on the platform. The “transformers” paper that
launched the modern AI boom
? Uploaded to arXiv. Same with the solution to the Poincaré conjecture, one of the seven Millennium Prize problems, famous for their difficulty and $1 million rewards. Just because a paper is posted on arXiv doesn’t mean it won’t appear in a prestigious journal someday, but it’s often where research makes its debut and stays openly available. The transformers paper is still routinely accessed via arXiv.
For scientists, imagining a world without arXiv is like the rest of us imagining one without public libraries or GPS. But a look at its inner workings reveals that it isn’t a frictionless utopia of open-access knowledge. Over the years, arXiv’s permanence has been threatened by everything from bureaucratic strife to outdated code to even, once, a spy scandal. In the words of Ginsparg, who usually redirects interview requests to an
FAQ document
—on arXiv, no less—and tried to talk me out of visiting him in person, arXiv is “a child I sent off to college but who keeps coming back to camp out in my living room, behaving badly.”

data.title: Don't force your kids to do math
data.author: happycats
data.article_summary: 文章主要讲述了一种不强迫孩子学习数学的育儿理念。作者认为数学应该是一种探索世界的方式，而不是任务。他通过游戏和日常生活中的小活动，让孩子在无压力的环境中自然接触数学，比如通过数楼梯、玩数字游戏和编故事等。他强调，孩子的自然好奇心很重要，家长应避免强行灌输知识，而是通过重复和趣味性引导孩子学习。作者还反思了平衡分享热情与施加压力之间的微妙界限，强调真正的目标是培养孩子对世界的好奇心和探索精神，而非仅仅追求学术成就。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何激发和培养对数学的兴趣和能力

不同观点：
• hahamaster认为数学应该像学习一门语言一样，通过听、理解、运用和识别模式来掌握，而不是单纯地死记硬背公式。他将学校教学比作教游客几句常用语，只停留在表面。
• jamesy0ung表示自己对数学缺乏兴趣，尤其因为数学在日常生活中应用有限，难以激励自己去学习。他更喜欢能立即看到成果的实践性学习，比如编程。
• CommenterPerson将学习数学比作学骑自行车，需要经过努力和挣扎才能掌握，并通过实践建立信心。他分享了自己的女儿通过早期练习最终在工程学取得成功的例子。
• smath介绍了“数学圈”的概念，强调培养好奇心，并分享了自己和孩子参与虚拟数学圈的经验。
• codemac主张通过一定的压力和强制练习来提高数学能力，认为家长的督促是孩子在数学等领域取得成功的关键因素。他引用了一项研究来支持自己的观点。
• SoftTalker分享了自己童年时通过奖励机制学习乘法的经验，认为这种方法有效。
• jerkstate推荐使用ChatGPT创建个性化的学习手册，并通过详细的例子帮助孩子理解数学概念。
• raymondgh感叹现代社会限制了孩子玩耍和探索的时间，暗示这对学习数学等领域有影响。
• r58lf推荐使用“Euclidea”应用来激发孩子对几何的兴趣，认为游戏化的学习方式更容易被接受。
• Infiniti20提到Kumon学习法，尽管自己不喜欢，但承认其有效性。
• asdf333也推荐数学圈，认为如果附近有这种活动值得参与。
• stuaxo提到通过观看教育节目“Number Blocks”来帮助孩子早期建立数学概念。
• IG_Semmelweiss建议通过数学游戏来激发孩子的兴趣，认为游戏能自然地促使孩子做数学题。
• helph67建议通过自然界中的例子，比如斐波那契数列，来让孩子理解数学的重要性。
• lanna分享了自己女儿从小对数学表现出浓厚兴趣并取得优异成绩的例子，暗示天赋和早期兴趣的重要性。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于是否应该通过强制练习和家长压力来提高数学能力。codemac支持这种方法，并引用研究支持，而其他评论者如 hahamaster和jamesy0ung则更强调兴趣和自主学习。
• 不同的方法和工具被推荐用来激发孩子的数学兴趣，包括应用程序、游戏、奖励机制和教育节目等。
• 数学在实际生活中的应用和其理论学习之间的脱节也被提及，jamesy0ung特别强调了这一点，并表示这影响了他的学习动机。
• 一些评论者分享了个人成功案例，如通过“数学圈”和观看教育节目来提高数学能力，提供了具体的实践建议。

43738195.article_content:
Wellâ¦ you probably shouldnât.
This is my one rule: if my son ever says he doesnât want to do math, we simply stop. No arguing, no bribing, no pushing. We do something else instead.
Why? Because math is not a choreâit’s a way of experiencing the world. Just like tasting new food, enjoying music, or feeling amazed by nature, math should always feel like play, never like work.
Kids are born explorers
. They naturally want to discover new things, including math. My main goal is simply to keep that natural curiosity alive and growing.
Before my son could even talkâas every parenting book suggestsâI talked to him constantly. Counting stairs, naming colors, explaining everything around us. I emphasized numbers because I genuinely enjoy them. And that’s perhaps the most important lesson I’ve learned:
children sense your true passions and naturally want to join in
.
Just play.
A simple wooden game
with numbers and colored bars was our playground. At first, it was sorting by colors or matching bars to numbers. Attention spans started short, a few moments here and there. But gradually, these moments grew into twenty or even thirty delightful minutes.
Watching him connect five bars to the numeral ‘5’ was magicalâit was the spark of mathematical abstraction. Soon, we created addition games and countless imaginative scenarios. I think I enjoyed inventing these simple, playful activities just as much as he did.
To keep math exciting, we built it into stories. For a while, I drew a burning house next to a 3x3 grid with missing numbers, sums waiting to be solved. Each correct answer earned him a blue pencil to draw water, putting out firesâhe loved pretending to be a fireman. Without realizing it, he was doing algebra. Train rides became great opportunities for these little games, free from distractions. Math is everywhere if you look for itâcalculating how much he could buy with 20 euros at the toy store, counting steps to reach a certain location, comparing which fruit is heavier at the market, or even timing how fast he could run across the park. You just need to open your child’s eyes to see math in daily life. Repetition is key!
The games evolved as he grew older. Card games like
Rat-a-Tat Cat
also became math gamesâadding card values became natural. Soon, calculations like 14 + 11 happened effortlessly in his head.
Repetition is key!
Time flying by is probably the sneakiest thing with kids. With our busy jobs, household chores, and daily demands, it’s easy to forget to spend meaningful time with your children. I have an internal KPI: if in the last three days I haven’t spent at least 30 minutes playing with my kid, there’s something seriously wrong.
Yet,
the hardest part remains balancing passion and pressure
. I deeply love math, coding, music, and sports, and naturally, I want to share these joys. But there’s a thin line between sharing and imposing. Children donât always express their discomfort openlyâfamily dynamics can be subtle and easily overlooked. Actually, this is one of the hardest things as a parent. It should be fine, but sometimes we don’t realize that sharing our passions might actually be about our own ego.
Understanding this is challenging, and we all fail at some point
. Still, it’s important to keep asking ourselves the question.
In fact, we stopped regularly engaging with structured math games before he started school at six, as his interests naturally shifted toward other exciting activities like building paper airplanes, painting, and drawingâthings that didnât interest him a year earlier. He’s probably above average at math, but that isn’t the point. What I genuinely cherish now is watching his curiosity spark questions about infinity. He wonders about adding infinities together and eagerly discusses different sizes of infinity with me, imagining them as creatures that can even ’eat’ each other.
Because, in the end,
the real goal isn’t math itself
âit’s nurturing a child’s natural eagerness to learn, explore, and wonder about the world.
Donât force math.

data.title: Consistent Hash Ring
data.author: jcartw
data.article_summary:
一致性哈希环（Consistent Hashing Ring）是一种用于分布式系统中数据分布和负载均衡的哈希算法。它将哈希值空间映射到一个环形结构上，范围从0到2^32-1。服务器节点通过哈希函数计算其哈希值，确定在环上的位置。数据也通过哈希函数确定位置，然后顺时针找到环上第一个节点作为存储位置，从而实现数据与服务器的稳定映射。

该算法的优点是在节点增加或移除时，只会影响相邻节点的数据分布，减少数据迁移成本。但在物理节点较少时，数据分布可能不均匀。为解决此问题，引入了虚拟节点（Virtual Nodes），将每个物理节点虚拟化为多个节点，均匀分布在环上，从而实现更均衡的负载和更高效的资源利用。通过调整虚拟节点数量，可以灵活实现负载均衡。

该工具提供可视化界面，用户可以通过添加、删除节点和调整虚拟节点数量，观察数据分布变化和算法效果。

Consistent Hashing Ring is a special hashing algorithm primarily used for data distribution and load balancing in distributed systems. It maps the hash value space onto a ring structure, ranging from 0 to 2^32-1. This approach allows us to better handle node addition and removal while minimizing data migration.
Basic Principles of Consistent Hashing Ring
The core concept of consistent hashing ring is to visualize the entire hash value space as a circular structure with its ends connected, ranging from 0 to 2^32-1. In this circular space, we first need to distribute server nodes around the ring. Each server node is assigned a position on the ring through a hash function that calculates its hash value.
When we need to store or retrieve data, we use the same hash function to calculate the data's hash value to determine its position on the ring.
After determining the data's position, we move clockwise along the ring until we encounter the first server node, which becomes the storage location for that data
. This mechanism ensures a stable and predictable mapping relationship between data and servers.
The elegance of this design lies in its handling of server node changes. When adding or removing server nodes, only the data distribution between adjacent nodes is affected, avoiding global data redistribution. This significantly reduces data migration costs during system scaling or node failures.
Why Virtual Nodes?
In practical applications, the basic hash ring has a notable issue:
when there are few server nodes, data distribution can become highly uneven
. This occurs because hash function results may not be uniformly distributed around the ring, causing some server nodes to handle more data while others remain relatively idle. This data skew seriously affects system performance and availability.
As shown in the figure below, with only 10 physical nodes and no virtual nodes, we can clearly observe the uneven data distribution. Each ring segment represents a node's data range, and different colored nodes show significantly different data proportions. For example, the green node handles 176 keys while the orange node has no data, creating a huge disparity that leads to overload on the green node while the orange node's resources remain idle, resulting in inefficient system resource utilization.
The root cause of this uneven distribution is that
with fewer nodes, hash function results may not be evenly distributed around the ring, leading to larger gaps between some nodes and smaller gaps between others
. Larger gaps mean that node must handle a larger data range and thus more requests. This problem is solved by introducing virtual nodes.
How Virtual Nodes Work
The core idea of virtual nodes is to virtualize each physical node into multiple virtual nodes. Specifically, the system creates multiple virtual replicas for each actual server node, with each virtual replica occupying a position on the hash ring.
While these virtual nodes occupy different positions on the ring, they all ultimately map to the same physical server
.
By introducing virtual nodes, we significantly increase the number of nodes on the ring, resulting in more uniform data distribution. For example, if we create 100 virtual nodes for each physical node, with just 4 physical nodes, we effectively have 400 distribution points on the ring. This approach effectively balances data load and reduces the risk of data skew. Additionally, the number of virtual nodes can be adjusted based on actual needs, providing more flexible load balancing capabilities.

data.title: Silicon Valley crosswalk buttons apparently hacked to imitate Musk, Zuck voices
data.author: coloneltcb
data.article_summary: 上周，美国加州中半岛地区的多个十字路口过街按钮遭到黑客入侵。当按下按钮时，会播放模仿马克·扎克伯格和埃隆·马斯克的声音。在红木城，一个声音自称是扎克伯格，称“将AI强制植入你的每个意识体验是正常的”，并说人们无法阻止。在帕洛阿尔托，一个声音假扮马斯克欢迎路人，并称“成为我的朋友就送你一辆Cybertruck”。另一个声音则发表了不当言论。随后，相关城市的政府部门关闭了受影响十字路口的语音功能，并表示此类篡改行为是非法的，存在安全隐患。加州交通局也确认部分受影响的信号灯已被停用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕高科技相关的恶作剧、黑客行为及其社会影响的讨论。

不同观点：
• [drillsteps5] 提到与马斯克声音克隆相关的问题，认为这些克隆声音没有正确的口音，并且在一些假视频中使用完美的美式口音，这让人产生怀疑。
• [reubenswartz] 以讽刺的口吻提到西雅图和杰夫·贝索斯，暗示富人利用其影响力操控公共事务。
• [jimmydoe] 关注技术实现，指出这些交叉口的配置可能通过应用程序进行，并猜测可能是由于认证泄露或物理篡改导致的。
• [magixx] 提出一种商业化的可能性，认为公司可能会开始租赁这些公共设施用于广告。
• [jpollock] 分享个人经验，指出多次按下这些设备可能会触发默认密码提示，暗示安全性问题。
• [userbinator] 支持政治讽刺，认为应有人反向黑入这些设备，但未明确支持违法行为。
• [ryandrake] 认为这是一种无害的恶作剧，且针对的是应受批评的人，并希望恶作剧者保持低调以免被抓。
• [fuzztester] 以幽默方式回应，使用双关语（高音/双关）。
• [lupusreal] 提出伦理问题，认为不应干扰残疾人士依赖的无障碍设备，表达了对这种行为的反对。
• [elpocko] 对一个技术论坛帖子的时间戳问题表示不满，认为这种操作令人不安，呼吁停止此类行为。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于恶搞高科技设备的行为是否合适，特别是涉及到公共设施和残疾人士使用的设备时，伦理问题变得尤为重要。
• 讨论还涉及到技术漏洞和安全性问题，如默认密码未更改等，显示出对公共设施网络安全的关注。
• 不同的观点在是否支持恶作剧和黑客行为上存在分歧，部分人认为这是无害的娱乐或讽刺，而另一些人则担心其潜在的负面影响和社会责任。

Getting your
Trinity Audio
player ready...
A crosswalk button in Redwood City plays a voice professing to be Mark Zuckerberg on April 12. Courtesy Justin Ward.
Crosswalk buttons along the mid-Peninsula were hacked last week so that when pressed, voices professing to be Mark Zuckerberg or Elon Musk began speaking.
Videos taken at locations in Redwood City, Menlo Park and Palo Alto showed various messages that began to play when crosswalk buttons were hit. The voices appeared to imitate how Zuckerberg and Musk sound.
In one video, taken on Saturday morning at the corner of Arguello Street, Broadway and Marshall Street in Redwood City, a voice claiming to be Zuckerberg says that “it’s normal to feel uncomfortable or even violated as we forcefully insert AI into every facet of your conscious experience. And I just want to assure you, you don’t need to worry because there’s absolutely nothing you can do to stop it.”
In another video, taken in downtown Palo Alto early on Saturday morning, a voice claiming to be Musk says that he would “like to personally welcome you to Palo Alto.”
“You know, people keep saying cancer is bad, but have you tried being a cancer? It’s f—— awesome,” the voice goes on to say.
A crosswalk button in Palo Alto plays a voice professing to be Elon Musk on April 12. Courtesy Cynthia Neuwalder.
Another video from downtown Palo Alto shows a voice impersonating Musk saying that he would give the listener a Cybertruck if they became his friend.
A crosswalk button in Menlo Park plays a voice professing to be Mark Zuckerberg on April 12. Courtesy Matthew Schluneker.
“You don’t know the level of depravity I would stoop to just for a crumb of approval,” the voice says. “I mean, let’s be real, it’s not like I had any moral convictions to begin with.”
Over in Menlo Park, a video taken near Meta’s headquarters shows a crosswalk signal with a voice identifying himself as “Zuck” stating how proud he is of “everything we’ve been building together.”
“From undermining democracy, to cooking our grandparents’ brains with AI slop, to making the world less safe for trans people, nobody does it better than us – and I think that’s pretty neat,” the voice says.
Some of the impacted crosswalk buttons in Palo Alto were no longer playing the messages on Saturday morning, one local resident reported.
City of Palo Alto spokesperson Meghan Horrigan-Taylor said on Saturday that city employees determined that 12 downtown intersections were impacted and have disabled the voice announcement feature on the crosswalks until repairs can be made. The tampering may have happened on Friday, Horrigan-Taylor said.
“Other traffic signals in the City were checked and the impact is isolated,” Horrigan-Taylor said. “Signal operations are otherwise unaffected, and motorists are reminded to always exercise caution around pedestrians.”
Redwood City Deputy City Manager Jennifer Yamaguma said on Monday that her city was aware of four locations where crosswalk signals were hacked.
“The unauthorized messages have since been disabled, and staff are evaluating ways to strengthen system protections,” Yamaguma said. “We also want to remind the public that tampering with City infrastructure, including crosswalk signals, is unlawful and poses a safety risk.”
Menlo Park spokesperson Kendra Calvert told this news organization that the affected crosswalks in Menlo Park are operated by the California Department of Transportation and that city-controlled crosswalks were not hacked.
Caltrans spokesperson Jeneane Crawford confirmed that crosswalks operated by the state transportation agency were impacted in Menlo Park and Palo Alto. Caltrans disabled the affected audio on Saturday morning, Crawford said.
“The pedestrian push buttons have been deactivated and crosswalks are currently operating on a timer,” Crawford said on Tuesday. “Caltrans is working with the supplier to determine a course of action so that the crosswalks are fully operational as quickly as possible.”
A Meta spokesperson referred questions to the cities with the impacted crosswalks. Tesla did not immediately reply to a request for comment.

• [userbinator] 支持政治讽刺，认为应有人反向黑入这些设备，但未明确支持违法行为。
• [ryandrake] 认为这是一种无害的恶作剧，且针对的是应受批评的人，并希望恶作剧者保持低调以免被抓。
• [fuzztester] 以幽默方式回应，使用双关语（高音/双关）。
• [lupusreal] 提出伦理问题，认为不应干扰残疾人士依赖的无障碍设备，表达了对这种行为的反对。
• [elpocko] 对一个技术论坛帖子的时间戳问题表示不满，认为这种操作令人不安，呼吁停止此类行为。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于恶搞高科技设备的行为是否合适，特别是涉及到公共设施和残疾人士使用的设备时，伦理问题变得尤为重要。
• 讨论还涉及到技术漏洞和安全性问题，如默认密码未更改等，显示出对公共设施网络安全的关注。
• 不同的观点在是否支持恶作剧和黑客行为上存在分歧，部分人认为这是无害的娱乐或讽刺，而另一些人则担心其潜在的负面影响和社会责任。

data.title: Notes on a claim that a mceliece348864 distinguisher uses only 2^529 operations [pdf]
data.author: nabla9
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Classic McEliece 密码算法的安全性及其在面对不同攻击算法时的表现

不同观点：
• Nabla9认为，[16] 中提到的成本计算（2529）远高于暴力搜索 256-bit 种子的成本，也比信息集合分解（ISD）方法的成本高。这表明该算法的代价过高，不具备实际攻击意义。
   
• Nabla9 指出，[16] 中讨论的算法仅用于区分公钥与随机数据，并未真正攻击基于OW-CPA（One-Wayness under Chosen-Plaintext Attack）的安全性假设。而Classic McEliece的安全性分析并不依赖于[16]中针对的可区分性假设，甚至在其安全性分析中明确声明不依赖此假设。

• Nabla9 进一步表示，[16] 错误地暗示了两个问题：（1）它攻击的是Classic McEliece依赖的安全性问题，而实际上并不是；（2）它比以往对Classic McEliece的最优攻击更快，但实际上并没有。

• Nabla9提到，在[16]出现后，他们立即做出了回应，但没有发布任何勘误。然而，现在有第三方开始引用[16]，声称这是对Classic McEliece的重要攻击进展。

补充讨论：
• [16]中提出的"syzygy distinguisher"方法是否对Classic McEliece的安全构成实际威胁存在争议。Nabla9认为该方法并未真正威胁到Classic McEliece的安全性假设，且其高昂的计算成本削弱了其实际攻击能力。

• 争议的焦点在于[16]是否错误地暗示了对Classic McEliece的有效攻击，以及第三方对其重要性的过度解读是否合理。

data.title: Authoritarian attitudes linked to altered brain anatomy, neuroscientists reveal
data.author: amichail
data.article_summary: 一项新的大脑成像研究发现，左右翼威权主义与大脑结构差异有关。右翼威权主义者在背内侧前额皮质的灰质体积较小，该区域与社交推理相关。极端左翼威权主义者则显示右侧前岛皮质的皮层厚度减少，该区域与同理心和情绪调节有关。研究还发现，左右翼威权主义者在情绪紧张时都表现得更冲动，但左翼威权主义者更易焦虑。研究旨在了解威权主义背后的神经生物学特征，并强调了政治光谱两端的僵化、反民主态度。

A new brain imaging study published in the journal
Neuroscience
has found that authoritarian attitudes on both the political left and right are linked to specific structural differences in the brain. Young adults who scored higher on right-wing authoritarianism had less gray matter volume in the dorsomedial prefrontal cortex, a region involved in social reasoning. Meanwhile, those who endorsed more extreme forms of left-wing authoritarianism showed reduced cortical thickness in the right anterior insula, a brain area tied to empathy and emotion regulation.
The research aimed to better understand the brain-based traits that might underlie authoritarian thinking. Previous studies have documented the psychological characteristics associated with authoritarianism—such as impulsivity, dogmatism, and heightened sensitivity to threat—but few have examined whether these traits are reflected in brain structure. The authors were particularly interested in both left- and right-wing authoritarianism, as research has increasingly recognized that rigid, anti-democratic attitudes can be found at both ends of the political spectrum.
“Research on ideological authoritarianism and other forms of radical political attitudes has been attracting growing attention,” said study author Jesús Adrián-Ventura, a professor at University of Zaragoza and member of
the Pseudo-Lab Research Group
.
“However, despite increasing reports on its psychological correlates, its integration with neurobiological data remains very limited, in particular regarding left-wing authoritarianism, which remains poorly represented in the current psychological literature. This led us to undertake a study on authoritarianism from a neuroscientific perspective.”
To investigate these questions, the researchers recruited 100 young adults in Spain, mostly university students between the ages of 18 and 30. Each participant completed a series of psychological questionnaires that measured political orientation, authoritarian beliefs, impulsivity, anxiety, and emotional regulation.
Importantly, the researchers used updated scales that assess both
traditional right-wing authoritarianism
and a recently developed
measure of left-wing authoritarianism
, which includes dimensions like anti-hierarchical aggression and top-down censorship.
Participants also underwent magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans using a high-resolution 3T scanner. The researchers focused on two structural features of the brain: gray matter volume, which reflects the density of neurons and connections in different brain regions, and cortical thickness, a measure of the depth of the brain’s outer layer. They used whole-brain statistical analyses to identify whether either of these features was associated with authoritarian beliefs.
Behaviorally, the results supported previous findings that people with authoritarian attitudes, regardless of political orientation, tend to act impulsively in emotionally charged situations. Both left-wing and right-wing authoritarians scored higher on “negative urgency,” a trait linked to impulsive actions under distress. However, left-wing authoritarianism—especially the tendency toward aggressive anti-establishment views—was also linked to higher levels of trait anxiety.
“Both left-wing and right-wing authoritarians act impulsively in emotionally negative situations, while the former tend to be more anxious,” Adrián-Ventura told PsyPost.
At the neural level, the researchers found two key structural associations. First, higher scores on right-wing authoritarianism were related to smaller gray matter volume in the dorsomedial prefrontal cortex. This region is known to be involved in understanding others’ perspectives, making moral judgments, and navigating complex social situations.
“Right-wing authoritarianism is associated with a lower dorsomedial prefrontal cortex gray matter volume, a region involved in understanding others’ thoughts and perspectives,” Adrián-Ventura said.
Previous studies have linked activity in this region to political decision-making and reactions to conflicting information. The authors suggest that reduced volume in this area might reflect more rigid thinking styles or difficulties with cognitive flexibility among right-wing authoritarians.
Second, individuals who scored high on the anti-hierarchical aggression component of left-wing authoritarianism showed lower cortical thickness in the right anterior insula. Interestingly, the same region has been implicated in studies examining reactions to political disagreement and emotional responses to moral violations.

data.title: Japan's big bet on stem-cell therapies might soon pay off
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 日本正接近实现干细胞疗法的医学突破。基于诺贝尔奖得主山中伸弥的研究，日本科学家正利用诱导多能干细胞（iPS细胞）开发治疗失明、心脏病和神经退行性疾病的方法。经过近二十年的研究和多次临床试验，许多早期结果显示这些疗法对帕金森病和脊髓损伤等疾病有效。日本政府和私营机构已投入巨资支持再生医学研究，目前全球有超过60项iPS细胞临床试验，其中近三分之一在日本。尽管治疗安全性已得到验证，且显示出疗效，但高昂的成本和大规模临床试验的缺乏仍是挑战。日本可能成为首个批准iPS细胞疗法的国家，最快可能在一年内实现。然而，公众对安全性的担忧和实际临床应用的限制仍需解决。

Japan’s big bet on stem-cell therapies might soon pay off with medical breakthroughs
Download PDF
Twitter
Facebook
Email
Illustration: Ricardo Santos; photographs: Ben Weller for
Nature
; Woodblock print: Utagawa Hiroshige (1831)
You have full access to this article via your institution.
Download PDF
Japan is brimming with signs of an approaching medical revolution. Shiny white robots are tending dishes of cells, rows of incubators hum in new facilities, and a deluxe, plush-carpeted hospital is getting ready to welcome its first patients.
Building on the Nobel-prizewinning work of stem-cell scientist Shinya Yamanaka, researchers across the country are crafting cells into strips of retina, sheets of cardiac muscle or blobs of neurons, in the hope of treating blindness, mending hearts and reversing neurodegeneration. Results from early-stage clinical trials — some announced just in the past few weeks — suggest that the cells might actually be working to treat conditions as varied as Parkinson’s disease and spinal-cord injury.
‘Big leap’ for Parkinson’s treatment: symptoms improve in stem-cells trials
Now, after nearly two decades of hard work and setbacks, many say that Japan is on the cusp of bringing these therapies to market.
Yamanaka, who runs a lab at Kyoto University, discovered in 2006 that adult cells
could be reprogrammed into an embryonic-like state
, capable of becoming practically any kind of tissue
1
. These induced pluripotent stem cells — or iPS cells — won Yamanaka the
Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 2012
, and propelled him to superstar status. They have become a symbol of the country’s global scientific aspirations.
The Japanese government has poured more than ¥110 billion (US$760 million today) into research and development on regenerative medicine, on top of billions more from private funders, organizations and companies. “People thought, ‘Now we can treat any incurable disease’,” says Shigeto Shimmura, director of Fujita Health University Haneda Clinic. “There was so much hype.”
Scientists launched clinical trials and start-up firms. Large biotech companies swooped in, investing even more in manufacturing hubs. Now, medical facilities are preparing to welcome a rush of patients from Japan and abroad. “Regenerative medicine in Japan is moving very dramatically,” says Masayo Takahashi, an ophthalmologist at Kobe City Eye Hospital and president of the biotechnology company, Vision Care. In 2014, she became the first to
treat someone with cells derived from iPS cells
.
Masayo Takahashi ran the first clinical trials for iPS cells.
Credit: Ben Weller for
Nature
There are
more than 60 iPS-cell clinical trials in progress worldwide
, nearly one-third of them in Japan. The treatments have proved to be safe and shown signs of benefit. Moreover, the technology has been improving apace, says Shimmura. And thanks to a fast-track approvals process for regenerative medicine, Japan could become the first country to approve iPS-cell-based treatments. This could happen within a year for Parkinson’s disease.
But those approvals are not yet in hand, treatment costs are high, large trials showing clear clinical benefit have yet to materialize, and concerns about safety could still sap the public’s willingness to try this treatment. “We’re down to realizing what the potential of these cells are, and what the limits are,” Shimmura says.
Eye see
Yamanaka’s iPS cells promised to bypass a bioethical stand-off that had threatened the potential of embryonic stem cells for a decade. Because production of iPS cells doesn’t require the destruction of human embryos, they were considered ethically less fraught. Furthermore, because they could be made from the cells of the person in need of treatment, they promised to offer transplantable tissues without the need for immune-suppressing drugs.
In 2014, Takahashi put this idea to the test. She took skin cells from a 70-year-old woman with a progressive eye condition known as macular degeneration and guided them into a younger, more pliable state using a recipe similar to the one Yamanaka had devised and refined. The resulting iPS cells were then grown into thin sheets of retinal cells and
transplanted into the woman’s eye
, where they have survived for ten years and prevented further vision loss, Takahashi says.
It was a procedure with practical limitations, however. Self-derived, or ‘autologous’, cell therapies are time-consuming and expensive to make, and the large cell-sheets that researchers crafted for implantation required intrusive surgery. Takahashi says she chose this approach to ensure the highest chance of clinical benefit — to demonstrate to the world what was possible. It was designed to be “scientifically, the best treatment”.
A technician at Vision Care in Kobe makes capillary tubes for injecting cells into the eye.
Credit: Ben Weller for
Nature

data.title: Unikernel Linux (UKL) (2023)
data.author: pabs3
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于将程序嵌入内核的不同技术方案和项目背景的讨论

不同观点：
• [rwmj 观点] 作为该项目的 former supervisor，对项目在 Hacker News 上出现表示意外。他提到项目由于研究资金枯竭已经停止。他表示愿意回答任何相关问题。
• [rzzzt 观点] 提到项目文档中的"references"部分引用了LKML（Linux Kernel Mailing List）讨论串和项目的GitHub仓库，提供了相关链接供进一步查阅。
• [phendrenad2 观点] 认为不需要使用该项目（unikernel Linux），可以通过将常规POSIX程序编译后嵌入内核镜像，使用 initramfs、initrd 或将其放在UEFI分区中。同时建议使用 busybox 或自定义的 init 进程来启动和监控程序。

补充讨论：
• phendrenad2 提出的方案与项目本身的方案形成对比，他主张使用现有的技术手段（如 initramfs、initrd）来实现类似功能，质疑了该项目（unikernel Linux）的必要性。
• rwmj 的评论提供了项目的背景信息，特别是关于资金问题导致项目中止，暗示项目在实际应用中可能面临资源限制。
• rzzzt 的评论提供了额外的技术资源链接，帮助进一步理解项目的技术细节，但没有直接评价项目的优劣。

争议焦点：
• 项目（unikernel Linux）是否具备实际应用中的优势和必要性。phendrenad2 明确表示现有技术已经可以满足需求，而项目本身的方案可能显得多余。
• 项目终止的原因可能涉及资金问题，这暗示了项目在实际推广和应用中可能面临的挑战。

data.title: Is it possible to write plain C iOS app in 2025?
data.author: iMario
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：是否可以使用纯C语言编写iOS应用程序，以及如何与Objective-C交互

不同观点：
• TazeTSchnitzel认为可以通过Objective-C的runtime函数用C语言编写iOS应用，尤其是使用SDL等库可以避免直接使用Objective-C。然而，使用Objective-C语法会更方便，某些核心框架如UIKit仍需Objective-C交互。
• Frieren指出，在跨平台开发中，C++更为常用，尤其是游戏开发。许多游戏引擎如Unity和Unreal使用C/C++作为核心代码，通过轻量级集成层进行系统调用。同时提到Electron等技术也是基于C++构建的。
• TheNewAndy分享了个人经验，表明使用SDL2可以在C语言中编写iOS游戏，且只需极少的Objective-C代码。
• colleagueRiley介绍了一个纯C调用MacOS API的项目，并提到他们创建了一个C语言的Objective-C包装器Silicon，但后来为了减少依赖而弃用。
• pjmlp反驳称，即使使用C语言编写，实际上仍需与Objective-C runtime交互，因此本质上还是在编写Objective-C应用。
• flohofwoe指出，通过包装Objective-C API可以在技术上实现，但直接使用Objective-C可能更方便。同时提到Apple提供的C++ Metal API和其他C语言头文件如Sokol。
• krackers支持手动翻译Objective-C调用，但承认无法避免与Objective-C runtime交互。
• enriquto推荐了一个可以跨平台编写图形程序的C语言库RGFW，并提供相关讨论链接。
• quelsolaar提到他们参与了一个自动包装C的Objective-C项目，并提供相关链接。
• throwaway2037提供了启发GitHub项目的StackOverflow问题链接。
• jokoon分享了在XCode中使用C++和Objective-C混合编程的经验。
• edg5000介绍了Objective-C++ (.mm扩展名) 的使用经验，指出可以通过C/C++调用iOS API，但仍需Objective-C进行某些路径操作。
• m463质疑是否可以在没有XCode的情况下编写macOS/iOS应用，并提到从C转向Objective-C的经验和XCode版本问题。
• Suppafly鼓励尝试GitHub上的项目。

data.title: Defold: cross-platform game engine
data.author: xd
data.article_summary: Defold是一款免费且开源的游戏引擎，专为高性能跨平台游戏开发设计。它无需配置，开箱即用，支持Lua脚本编程和多种编辑器功能，如视觉编辑器、粒子编辑器和瓦片地图编辑器。Defold允许使用单一代码库发布游戏到多个平台，包括PlayStation、Nintendo Switch、Android、iOS、Windows等。引擎集成了Atom、VS Code、Rive、Spine等工具，并提供免费的云构建和扩展功能。Defold拥有活跃的开发社区和定期的版本更新，并提供技术支持选项。此外，引擎还被用于多款成功游戏的开发，如《Family Island》。用户可以从官方教程、手册和API参考中学习使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Defold引擎的许可证模式、功能特点及其与其他引擎的比较

不同观点：
• [支持观点] evv和progbits对Defold的许可证模式表示赞赏，认为其明确区分了“源代码可用”（source-available）和“开源”（Open Source），避免了误用。他们特别指出，该许可证允许开发者对引擎进行专有修改，且无需公开这些修改，同时还能自由地将使用该引擎开发的游戏商业化。这种安排被认为是公平且经过深思熟虑的。

• [技术实现] tunaoftheland对Defold的技术实现表示赞赏，尤其是其GUI编辑器使用了Clojure语言，并提到了Defold来源于瑞典的一家游戏工作室（King），具有商业发布的背景。这显示了Defold在技术选型上的独特性。

• [与Godot的比较] rockyj、nunodonato和LichenStone提到了Defold与Godot的比较，指出Godot在社区支持、文档和3D功能方面可能更为先进，而Defold的优势在于其多平台导出能力，尤其是在主机支持方面。

• [编程语言偏好] bentt对Defold使用Lua而不是C#表示了一些失望，但仍然认为它比需要完全用C++重新编译的引擎要好。synergy20提到了Teal语言（类似于TypeScript与JavaScript的关系），但并未深入讨论其使用广泛性。

• [与其他引擎的比较] 2mlWQbCK将Defold与Löve 2D进行了比较，指出Defold支持更多平台，但提及了这些平台可能附带的非开放依赖。此外，rockyj还提到了其他引擎如MonoGame、Unity和Unreal，认为选择引擎时需考虑学习投入、功能需求和平台支持等因素。

补充讨论：
• [平台支持] rootnod3提到Defold支持PS4/5和Switch，但未提及FreeBSD，质疑其对FreeBSD的支持情况。

• [特定应用] imzadi关注Defold在VR开发方面的支持情况，但未找到明确答案。

• [安装便捷性] tombert提到Defold尚未在Nixpkgs中，并提供了一个相关链接。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议点在于Defold使用的Lua语言是否适合开发者，以及其与Godot等其他引擎在功能和社区支持方面的比较。一些开发者可能更偏好C#等其他编程语言，而Godot在3D功能和社区支持上可能更具优势。

data.title: Google is illegally monopolizing online advertising tech, judge rules
data.author: IdealeZahlen
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：谷歌广告业务是否构成垄断，以及是否应该对其进行拆分

不同观点：
• [megaman821] 认为谷歌的广告业务可以被拆分，而不必摧毁谷歌本身。谷歌在广告空间销售、广告拍卖和广告投放中扮演多重角色，但部分业务确实可以分离。
• [Frieren] 主张谷歌应在多年前就被拆分，现在采取行动为时已晚。许多大公司通过垄断市场来控制中间环节，损害了客户和供应商的利益。谷歌、苹果、亚马逊和Uber等公司都采用类似策略，这种情况应被法律禁止。
• [ApolloFortyNine] 对谷歌是否构成广告垄断表示怀疑，认为谷歌作为平台的所有者，有权决定收费标准，且用户并非被迫使用谷歌。同时指出，iOS应用商店才是真正的垄断，因为没有其他途径在iOS上发布应用。
• [nixpulvis] 希望看到有公司通过提供不具侵入性的广告来竞争，认为质量高的广告会带来更好的用户体验和网站流量。
• [guywithahat] 反对针对谷歌的行动，认为市场上已有众多搜索引擎选择，且AI技术正在削弱谷歌的优势。谷歌的成功源于其优秀的服务，而非垄断。
• [internetter] 对谷歌广告业务成为反垄断目标感到意外，但认为谷歌的一些辅助服务（如Chrome）确实是反垄断的合适目标。
• [matthest] 支持FTC打击垄断，但认为应优先处理医疗保险市场的垄断问题，因为这更直接影响美国人的生活质量。
• [ashu1461] 对此次行动是否会有实际效果表示怀疑，认为过去类似声明未带来实质变化。
• [throwaway743] 提到谷歌旗下的AdMob存在问题，如邮件功能多年未修复，且在问题归咎于谷歌时，开发者往往无法得到补偿。
• [xhkkffbf] 建议谷歌主动提出拆分计划，认为像Ma Bell那样的拆分可能会带来更好的竞争与合作。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于谷歌广告业务是否构成垄断，以及是否应通过法律手段进行拆分。部分观点认为谷歌通过其平台优势控制市场，损害了其他市场参与者的利益；而另一些观点则认为谷歌的成功源于其优秀的服务，且市场中仍有其他选择。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是关于医疗保险市场的垄断问题，部分评论认为这是更紧迫且对消费者影响更大的问题，应优先处理。
• 还有人关注广告质量和用户体验的问题，认为如果能有公司提供不具侵入性的广告，可能会带来更好的市场竞争。

data.title: arXiv moving from Cornell servers to Google Cloud
data.author: ColinWright
data.article_summary: arXiv, part of Cornell Tech, is hiring for several software development positions as it transitions its services to the cloud (Google Cloud). This includes roles such as general software engineers, DevOps specialists, and a scientist/software developer. The cloud transition aims to improve scalability, modernize infrastructure, and enhance services like metadata collection and author identity management. Visa sponsorship is not available, and candidates must have the legal right to work in the U.S. Preference is given to those able to work on-site at Cornell Tech's NYC campus, though hybrid/remote options may be considered. The roles involve re-architecting systems, containerization, improving monitoring, and establishing robust CI/CD pipelines. The overall goal is to expand arXiv's subject coverage and enhance accessibility and usability for the research community.

  - **x_may**：认为Arxiv从资本支出（Capex）转向运营支出（Opex）是科技公司的常见做法，猜测Google Cloud Platform（GCP）可能在资助该项目，并怀疑这是GCP通过支付服务费用换取合作和宣传的策略。
  - **tokai**：反对引入Google，主张建立国际学术图书馆联盟来运营Arxiv，认为科学出版不应由私营企业控制。

• **资金来源与可持续性**：
  - **kevinventullo**：建议设立非营利组织来支持Arxiv的运营，并表示愿意捐款。
  - **kiproping**：提到Arxiv的历史和围绕它的争议，暗示可能与创始人Ginsparg的退休有关。
  - **sppfly**：关注谁将支付Google的服务费用，并希望Arxiv继续免费提供服务。

• **技术与招聘问题**：
  - **gcr**：指出Cornell大学目前处于招聘冻结状态，相关职位可能无法填补。
  - **andyjohnson0**：认为技术升级主要是由于技能短缺和招聘问题，并指出即使转向Google，Arxiv仍可能受到恶意资金干扰。
  - **dig1**：怀疑Arxiv的技术升级是被Google说服或误导，担心简单的架构被复杂且昂贵的云服务取代。

补充讨论：
• **地缘政治与访问限制**：
  - **darkoob12**：担心像伊朗这样的国家会被封锁，认为互联网正被美国公司控制，决定内容和访问权限。

• **政治风险与管理问题**：
  - **perihelions**：提出Arxiv是否受到美国政府对Cornell的敌对行动影响，并担心Cornell可能因此无法继续运营Arxiv。

• **用户体验与技术改进**：
  - **Daviey**：对技术升级表示欢迎，认为如果能够改善用户体验（如无需伪造用户代理即可下载论文），则值得高兴。

• **控制权与企业影响**：
  - **dvrp**：希望Arxiv保持不依赖特定供应商。
  - **einpoklum**：担心公共基础设施被大公司（尤其是Alphabet）控制，认为这是不利的趋势。

争议焦点：
- **引入Google云服务的利弊**：一方认为这是技术升级和运营优化的必要步骤，另一方担心私营企业控制公共学术资源，以及由此带来的成本和访问问题。

43726640.article_content:
Careers at arXiv
arXiv is part of Cornell Tech, the graduate campus and research center of Cornell University. All arXiv employees are Cornell University employees.
Positions at arXiv are
staff positions with benefits (endowed)
.
Visa sponsorship is not available. You must already possess the legal right to work in the US.
arXiv is headquartered at the
Cornell Tech campus on Roosevelt Island in New York City
. When hiring, there is a strong preference for candidates who can report to work at that location, but hybrid and/or remote work may be an option.
Software development
We are already underway on the arXiv CE ("Cloud Edition") project. This is a project to re-home all arXiv services from VMs at Cornell to a cloud provider (
Google Cloud
). There are a number of reasons for this transition, including improving arXiv's scalability while modernizing our infrastructure. This will not be a simple port of the existing arXiv code base because this project will:
replace the portion of our backends still written in perl and PHP
re-architect our article processing to be fully asynchronous, and provide better insight into the processing workflows
containerize all, or nearly all arXiv services so we can deploy via Kubernetes or services like
Google Cloud Run
improve our monitoring and logging facilities so we can more quickly identify and manage production issues with arxiv.org
create a robust CI/CD pipeline to give us more confidence that changes we deploy will not cause services to regress
The cloud transition is a pre-requisite to modernizing arXiv as a service. The modernization will enable:
- arXiv to expand the subject areas that we cover
- improve the metadata we collect and make available for articles, adding fields that the research community has requested such as funder identification
- deal with the problem of ambiguous author identities
- improve accessibility to support users with impairments, particularly visual impairments
- improve usability for the entire arXiv community
We have three SWE openings, one general and two specialized
Software Engineer
This person should be a software generalist, who can work in a variety of environments, programming languages, frontend and backend. Should have web development and SQL experience.
Software Engineer IV
(Software Engineer)
DevOps Specialist
We are looking for a developer with Cloud DevOps experience to lead the effort of modernizing our devops system so we can efficiently, reliably, and securely deploy new code, using Infrastructure as code principles. This task will likely involve a fair amount of automation via
gitops
, as well as Google Cloud Platform tools. The devops lead will also put in place a robust CI/CD pipeline, and may also be asked to help fill in test cases.
DevOps Software Engineer
Scientist/Software Developer
We're looking for someone with serious software development skills who has also used arXiv for scientific research, and preferably someone who has authored arXiv submissions. We expect this person to represent and be an advocate for the interests of all scientists, within the arXiv software development team (no pressure!). We believe there are lots of you scientists-turned-software-developers out there. Please apply!
Software Engineer Scientist
43726640.article_summary: arXiv, part of Cornell Tech, is hiring for several software development positions as it transitions its services to the cloud (Google Cloud). This includes roles such as general software engineers, DevOps specialists, and a scientist/software developer. The cloud transition aims to improve scalability, modernize infrastructure, and enhance services like metadata collection and author identity management. Visa sponsorship is not available, and candidates must have the legal right to work in the U.S. Preference is given to those able to work on-site at Cornell Tech's NYC campus, though hybrid/remote options may be considered. The roles involve re-architecting systems, containerization, improving monitoring, and establishing robust CI/CD pipelines. The overall goal is to expand arXiv's subject coverage and enhance accessibility and usability for the research community.
